definition_zh: 开关；转换；转变；调换
definition_en: a device that turns power on or off, or a change from one thing to another
core_image: 手指按下墙上的开关，房间立刻亮起
scene: 她按下开关，灯亮了。 She pressed the switch and the light came on.
sceneCN: 这里 switch 是「开关」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她按下开关，灯亮了。

senses.title: A device for turning power on and off
senses.definition: a small device that starts or stops an electric current
senses.definitionCN: 启动或切断电流的小装置
senses.example: She pressed the switch and the light came on.
senses.exampleCN: 她按下开关，灯亮了。
senses.why: The word first named a thin twig, and a twig flicked to make contact gave the electric device its name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指细树枝，用树枝轻弹接通电路的装置因此得名。

senses.title: To change to something else
senses.definition: to change from one thing or system to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种事物或系统改为另一种
senses.example: We switched to a cheaper supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 我们换成了更便宜的供应商。
senses.why: Flicking a switch changes the state at once, so any quick change is called a switch.
senses.whyCN: 拨动开关立刻改变状态，于是任何快速改变都叫 switch。

senses.title: A change or exchange
senses.definition: an act of changing from one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一事物转为另一事物的行为
senses.example: There has been a switch in policy.
senses.exampleCN: 政策出现了转变。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the change itself, as often happens in English.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词指这种改变本身，这在英语里很常见。

senses.title: To exchange one for another
senses.definition: to exchange the positions of two things
senses.definitionCN: 互换两个事物的位置
senses.example: They switched seats before the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开场前他们换了座位。
senses.why: Two poles of a switch swap contact, so swapping places is a natural extension.
senses.whyCN: 开关的两极交换接触，因此互换位置是自然引申。

definition_zh: 之后；随后；后来；不久之后；以后
definition_en: at a later time, especially after an event that has just been mentioned
core_image: 事情过去以后，脚步声才在后面慢慢响起来
scene: 会议结束，人们收拾文件陆续离开，走廊里安静下来。 We walked to the station afterwards.
sceneCN: 这里 afterwards 是「之后」（第 1 个义项：紧接刚提到的事情之后）；句意为散会之后我们步行去了车站。画面里可辨认的是会议桌、文件和空走廊。

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写，去掉了副词属格词尾 -s，义同「之后；后来」
由 after 加 word 复合而成的名词，义为「后记；跋」，与 afterwards 拼写相近，但构词来源不同

senses.title: Just after an event
senses.definition: after an event that has just been mentioned, especially immediately after it
senses.definitionCN: 在刚刚提到的那件事之后，尤指紧接着其后
senses.example: We had lunch and afterwards walked along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃了午饭，随后沿着海岸散步。
senses.why: Afterward began as æfterweard, 'towards the rear'; the later event stands behind the one just named, so afterwards marks what comes in the rear.
senses.whyCN: afterward 最初是 æfterweard「朝后方」，后发生的事站在刚提到的事背后，所以 afterwards 标记的是落在后面的那一件事。

senses.title: Later, after some time
senses.definition: at a later time, often after a noticeable interval, when looking back
senses.definitionCN: 在较晚的时候，常指隔了一段明显的间隔，多用于回顾
senses.example: She moved to another city and afterwards rarely called.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬到另一座城市，后来就很少打电话了。
senses.why: If the 'rear' lies far behind, the gap between the two events widens, and the word slides from 'next' to 'later on'.
senses.whyCN: 如果「后方」落在很远的地方，两件事之间的间隔就被拉开，词义也从「接着」滑向「后来」。

senses.title: Shortly after, with soon or shortly
senses.definition: used with soon, shortly or immediately to stress that very little time passed
senses.definitionCN: 与 soon、shortly 或 immediately 连用，强调经过的时间极短
senses.example: Shortly afterwards, the lights in the hall went out.
senses.exampleCN: 不久之后，大厅里的灯灭了。
senses.why: The interval is the only variable in the word, so an adverb that measures it can shrink the gap to almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词唯一的变量就是间隔长短，所以加上衡量间隔的副词，就能把间隔压到几乎为零。

senses.title: At a later point in the future
senses.definition: at a time after something that is still to happen, seen from the present
senses.definitionCN: 站在现在看，在某件尚未发生的事情之后的某个时间
senses.example: We can discuss the details afterwards, once the guests have gone.
senses.exampleCN: 等客人走了以后，我们可以再谈细节。
senses.why: The same 'behind' image works for a future event: the talk lies behind the dinner that has not yet taken place.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「在后面」的图像也适用于将来的事：谈话落在还没发生的晚餐之后，于是 afterwards 指「以后」。

intro.en: Afterwards is afterward plus an old adverbial ending, and its history begins with a purely spatial word.
intro.cn: afterwards 是 afterward 加上一个古老的副词词尾，它的历史从一个纯空间词开始。

items.en: Æfter meant 'after, behind', and it forms the first element of the compound.
items.cn: æfter 意为「在……之后、在后面」，构成这个复合词的前半部分。

items.en: The suffix -weard meant 'turned towards', as in modern towards and homeward.
items.cn: 后缀 -weard 意为「朝向」，现代英语的 towards 与 homeward 仍保留这个成分。

items.en: Æfterweard meant 'behind, in the rear', a spatial adverb with no time sense yet.
items.cn: æfterweard 意为「在后面、朝后方」，当时还是一个纯空间副词，尚无时间义。

items.en: The meaning moved from place to time, and afterward came to mean 'later, after that'.
items.cn: 词义从空间移到时间，afterward 开始表示「后来、在那之后」。

items.en: An adverbial genitive -s was added, giving afterwards; the exact first date of this form is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词属格词尾 -s 被加上，形成 afterwards；这个形式的确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the American spelling, a look-alike compound and two adverbs built with -wards; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of later time.
note.cn: 形近组收美式拼写、一个形近复合词与两个以 -wards 结尾的副词；近义组收表示较晚时间的副词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same adverb, without the final s.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后、后来」，是本词的美式拼写，去掉了末尾的 s。

entries.definition: A short section at the end of a book; formed from after and word, not from this adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后记、跋」，由 after 与 word 复合而成；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning in the direction of; it shares the adverbial -s ending but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝、向」，同样带副词属格词尾 -s，但词根不同。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning forward in time or space; built with the same -wards ending.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向前、以后」，构词时用的是同一个 -wards 词尾，但词根不同。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after the moment being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来、稍后」，只强调时间较晚，不强调紧接着。

entries.definition: Afterwards, in a formal or report style.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「随后、之后」，语气正式，多用于报告与叙述。

entries.definition: After that time, often suggesting a continuing state; more formal and more bookish.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此后」，常暗示某种状态持续下去，语气比 afterwards 更书面。

entries.definition: Immediately after this one, in a sequence; it looks forward rather than back.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「紧接着、下一个」，强调次序上的紧邻，方向朝前而不是回顾。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real route from æfterweard to afterwards and the phrases that measure the gap.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子沿着从 æfterweard 到 afterwards 的真实路径，并配合衡量间隔的常见说法。

normal.en: Afterwards is afterward plus the adverbial -s, the same ending as in towards and onwards.
normal.cn: afterwards 是 afterward 加副词词尾 -s，与 towards、onwards 的结尾相同。

normal.en: The oldest form, æfterweard, meant 'towards the rear', a purely spatial picture.
normal.cn: 最古老的形式 æfterweard 意为「朝后方」，是纯空间的图像。

normal.en: American English usually drops the s and writes afterward.
normal.cn: 美式英语通常去掉 s，写作 afterward。

normal.en: Shortly afterwards and soon afterwards measure the gap between the two events.
normal.cn: shortly afterwards 与 soon afterwards 都在衡量两件事之间的间隔。

normal.en: The word never takes an object: it stands alone after the event has been named.
normal.cn: 这个词从不带宾语：事情点明之后，它自己单独站着。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs, and you sit in the second one only after the first is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子，第一把空了，你才坐到第二把上。

abstract.en: The distance between the chairs can be a step or a year; the word does not care.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子之间的距离可以是一步，也可以是一年，这个词并不计较。

abstract.en: When the second chair is far away, afterwards quietly turns into 'later'.
abstract.cn: 当第二把椅子很远时，「之后」就悄悄变成了「后来」。

examples.en: We had lunch and afterwards walked along the shore.
examples.cn: 我们吃了午饭，随后沿着海岸散步。

examples.en: She moved to another city and afterwards rarely called.
examples.cn: 她搬到另一座城市，后来就很少打电话了。

examples.en: Shortly afterwards, the lights in the hall went out.
examples.cn: 不久之后，大厅里的灯灭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夫特沃兹」——脚步总落在事情后头：之后；隔得久了就成了后来。

root: 由 afterward 加副词属格 -s 构成。afterward 来自古英语 æfterweard「朝后方」，由 æfter「在后」加 -weard「朝向」构成；词义从中古英语起由空间转向时间，-s 是英语副词属格词尾，与 towards、onwards 同类。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses measure one distance: how far behind the mentioned event the next thing stands, from the very next moment to a point in the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都在量同一段距离：下一件事落在刚提到的事情后面多远，可以近在下一刻，也可以远到将来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: once the event is over, footsteps sound behind it, at a distance that can be short or long.
core.cn: 核心意象：事情结束之后，脚步声才在后面响起，距离可近可远。

branches.en: THE NEXT THING: the following event stands directly behind the one just named.
branches.cn: 紧接着：后面那件事就贴在刚提到的事背后。

branches.en: THE WIDE GAP: when the rear is far off, the word reads as 'later'.
branches.cn: 长间隔：后方离得远时，词义就读作「后来」。

branches.en: THE NARROW GAP: soon and shortly shrink the distance to almost nothing.
branches.cn: 短间隔：soon 与 shortly 把这段距离压到几乎为零。

branches.en: THE FUTURE: the same rear position can be projected onto events not yet happened.
branches.cn: 将来线：同一个「后方」也能投射到尚未发生的事情上。

branches.en: ONE MEASURE: every sense asks the same question, how far behind the mentioned event the next one lies.
branches.cn: 同一把尺：所有义项问的都是同一个问题——下一件事落在刚提到的事后面多远。

intro.en: Afterwards is afterward plus an ending, and every element in it is native English.
intro.cn: afterwards 是 afterward 加一个词尾，其中每个成分都是英语本族成分。

latinIntro.en: The word is entirely Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so this column is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全来自日耳曼语，没有拉丁语同源词，所以这一栏留空。

items.example: It is the first half of the old compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个古老复合词的前半截。

items.example: It gives the compound its direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给这个复合词一个方向。

items.example: The old form was spatial before it was temporal.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老形式先有空间义，后有时间的义。

items.example: The word lost its final s in American spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在美式拼写中少了末尾的 s。
它把 afterward 变成 afterwards。

items.example: It is the modern form of the old suffix.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个古老后缀的现代形式。

items.meaning: in the direction of, as an adverb
items.example: It appears in towards and onwards.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 towards 与 onwards 中。

items.example: It is the living first element of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词仍然活跃的前半部分。

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写，去掉副词属格词尾 -s，义同「之后；后来」
由 after 加 word 复合而成，义为「后记；跋」，与 afterwards 拼写相近但构词来源不同

definition_zh: 精确的；准确的；严格的
definition_en: completely correct and precise
core_image: 一把刻度清晰到毫米的尺子
scene: 木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。 The carpenter measured twice before drawing the exact cutting line on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 exact 是「精确的」（第 1 个义项：每个细节都完全正确）；句意：木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。

senses.title: Completely correct
senses.definition: completely correct in every detail
senses.definitionCN: 每个细节都完全正确
senses.example: The exact time is ten past five.
senses.exampleCN: 确切时间是五点十分。
senses.why: Exact comes from Latin exigere, to weigh precisely.
senses.whyCN: exact 源自拉丁语 exigere（精确称量）。

senses.title: Strict
senses.definition: demanding great care and accuracy
senses.definitionCN: 要求高度细致准确
senses.example: The exact rules must be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 必须遵守严格的规定。
senses.why: Precise measurement becomes strict demand.
senses.whyCN: 精确的衡量变成严格的要求。

senses.title: To demand
senses.definition: to demand and obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 索取并得到某物
senses.example: The teacher exacted an apology from the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要求全班道歉。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old sense of demanding payment.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了索取偿付的旧义。

intro.en: Exact comes from Latin exactus, past participle of exigere, to drive out or weigh.
intro.cn: exact 源自拉丁语 exactus，是 exigere（驱出、称量）的过去分词。

items.en: Agere means to drive or do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: Exigere means to drive out or weigh.
items.cn: exigere 意为驱出或称量。

items.en: Exactus means precise or exacted.
items.cn: exactus 意为精确的或被索取的。

items.en: Exact first describes precise measurement.
items.cn: exact 最初描述精确的测量。

items.en: It also means strict or demanding.
items.cn: 它也指严格或苛求的。

note.en: Exact stresses full correctness; precise stresses fine detail.
note.cn: exact 强调完全正确；precise 强调细节精细。

entries.definition: in a precise way
the quality of being exact
demanding great care
exact in every detail
correct in all details
right and without mistakes

normalIntro.en: Exact is a ruler marked down to the smallest line.
normalIntro.cn: exact 是一把刻度细到最小格的尺子。

normal.en: Exact time means the precise hour and minute.
normal.cn: exact time 意为确切的小时和分钟。

normal.en: Exact words means the very words used.
normal.cn: exact words 意为原原本本的话。

normal.en: To be exact means to speak precisely.
normal.cn: to be exact 意为确切地说。

normal.en: An exact match fits perfectly.
normal.cn: an exact match 完全吻合。

normal.en: Compare precise: exact stresses no error, precise stresses fine detail.
normal.cn: 对比 precise：exact 强调无误差，precise 强调细节精细。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with marks down to a millimeter.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刻度细到毫米的尺子。

abstract.en: Imagine two puzzle pieces fitting without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图严丝合缝。

abstract.en: Think of a key that turns only in one lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只在一把锁里转动的钥匙。

examples.en: Can you give me the exact date?
examples.cn: 你能告诉我确切的日期吗？

examples.en: Those were his exact words.
examples.cn: 那就是他的原话。

examples.en: The work demands exact measurements.
examples.cn: 这项工作要求精确的测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exact」读起来短促干脆——像尺子一下卡到位，分毫不差。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量、要求）→ exactus（精确的）→ exact，核心义「量得准、要求严」。

sensesIntro.en: Exact starts with complete correctness, extends to strict demands, and keeps a verb sense of demanding.
sensesIntro.cn: exact 从完全正确开始，延伸到严格要求，还保留索取的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked down to a millimeter.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度细到毫米的尺子。

branches.en: Complete correctness is the core.
branches.cn: 完全正确是核心含义。

branches.en: Precision can become strictness.
branches.cn: 精确可以变成严格。

branches.en: The verb means to demand.
branches.cn: 动词意为强求。

branches.en: A measured standard and a strict rule meet.
branches.cn: 精确标准与严格规则相遇。

branches.en: Demanding payment and exact measuring share a root.
branches.cn: 索取与精确称量共享同一个词根。

intro.en: Exact joins ex-, out, to the Latin root ag, to drive.
intro.cn: exact 由 ex-（出）与拉丁词根 ag（驱动）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 是直接来源。

definition_zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序；（计算机）优先级
definition_en: the state of being more important than something else, or a thing that is ranked first
core_image: 急诊分诊台上，红色标签的伤员先被推进手术室
scene: 医院分诊时，护士把红黄绿标签贴在病历夹上。 The triage nurse set the priority of each patient by colour, so the most serious cases were seen first.
sceneCN: 这里 priority 是「优先次序、优先级」（第 3 个义项：按重要性排出的先后顺序）；句意：分诊护士用颜色给每位病人排定优先次序，最危重的先看。图中可辨识物件：分诊台、红黄绿标签、担架、病历夹、时钟；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序

derivatives.zh: 优先处理；按优先级排序

senses.title: The thing ranked first
senses.definition: the thing that is treated as most important
senses.definitionCN: 被当作最重要的事情
senses.example: Patient safety is our top priority.
senses.exampleCN: 病人安全是我们的头等大事。
senses.why: Priority is the noun of prior: it names whatever stands first in a line. In modern management, that first thing is often called a priority in the plural.
senses.whyCN: priority 是 prior 的名词：它命名排在队伍最前的东西。现代管理中，这个“第一之物”常用复数 priorities 表示。

senses.title: The state of being more important
senses.definition: the condition of having a stronger claim than others
senses.definitionCN: 拥有比其余更强的地位
senses.example: The issue has priority over all others.
senses.exampleCN: 这个议题优先于其余一切。
senses.why: The word can name a status rather than a thing: something has priority. It is a relation, not an object, and it always implies competitors.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名状态而非事物：某物具有 priority。它是一种关系，不是物件，而且总隐含竞争者。

senses.title: An order of precedence
senses.definition: a ranking that decides what is handled first
senses.definitionCN: 决定先处理什么的排序
senses.example: The committee set its priorities for the year.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会定下了年度优先次序。
senses.why: Once several items compete, priority becomes a list. The plural is natural here: a set of ranked claims, not one favourite.
senses.whyCN: 一旦多项事务竞争，priority 就变成一份列表。复数在此很自然：一组被排序的诉求，而非一个宠儿。

senses.title: The right to go first
senses.definition: the right of a vehicle or person to move before others
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或人先于他人行动的权利
senses.example: Bicycles have priority at this crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车在这个路口有优先通行权。
senses.why: Traffic rules codify the line: priority marks who may move first. The metaphor becomes legal and physical at the same time.
senses.whyCN: 交通规则把队伍编码：priority 标记谁可以先动。这个隐喻同时变成法律与物理的。

senses.title: Ceremonial precedence
senses.definition: the rank order of people at a formal occasion
senses.definitionCN: 正式场合中人们的位次顺序
senses.example: The ambassador's priority in the procession was fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 大使在行列中的位次是固定的。
senses.why: Court and diplomacy rank bodies in space: who enters first, who sits nearest. Priority is the abstract name for that spatial order.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷与外交按空间给人排序：谁先进、谁坐得最近。priority 是那种空间秩序的抽象名称。

senses.title: A computing priority level
senses.definition: a value that decides how soon a task is serviced
senses.definitionCN: 决定任务多快被处理的一个值
senses.example: The process runs at high priority.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进程以高优先级运行。
senses.why: Operating systems borrow the queue image: every task waits, and priority decides who jumps ahead. It is the same ranking, made numeric.
senses.whyCN: 操作系统借用排队意象：每个任务都在等，优先级决定谁插到前面。还是同一个排序，只是变成数字。

senses.title: Top priority
senses.definition: the single most urgent item, in the phrase top priority
senses.definitionCN: 短语 top priority：唯一最紧迫的事项
senses.example: Rebuilding the bridge is a top priority.
senses.exampleCN: 重建桥梁是首要任务。
senses.why: Top priority doubles the ranking: top already means first, priority already means first. The redundancy marks urgency, which is why it is so common in politics.
senses.whyCN: top priority 重复了排序：top 已是第一，priority 已是第一。这种冗余标记紧迫性，所以它在政治语言中如此常见。

senses.title: Low priority
senses.definition: an item that can wait, in the phrase low priority
senses.definitionCN: 短语 low priority：可以等待的事项
senses.example: The paint job is a low priority this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年粉刷是次要事项。
senses.why: The scale runs from top to low. Low priority is not unimportant but postponable: the item stays in the queue, just further back.
senses.whyCN: 这个尺度从 top 到 low。low priority 不是不重要，而是可推迟：事项仍在队列里，只是更靠后。

senses.title: Earlier status in time (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, the state of being earlier in time
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：在时间上更早的状态
senses.example: The priority of the claim depended on its date.
senses.exampleCN: 这项权利的在先性取决于它的日期。
senses.why: The oldest sense was temporal: priority meant being earlier. Modern English keeps the temporal trace mainly in law, where an earlier filing wins.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是时间性的：priority 指更早。现代英语主要在法律中保留时间痕迹：先提交者胜。

intro.en: Priority is the noun of prior, formed in Medieval Latin as prioritas. It began as 'the state of being earlier' and grew into 'the right to be first', which is why both time and rank live inside it.
intro.cn: priority 是 prior 的名词，在中世纪拉丁语中作 prioritas。它始于“更早的状态”，发展为“居先的权利”，所以时间与等级都住在它里面。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'the state of being earlier or prior'.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“更早或在先的状态”。

items.en: From prioritas 'priority, precedence', from Latin prior 'former, first of two'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas“优先、居先”，源出拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”。

items.en: prior is a comparative of *pri- 'before', from PIE *per- 'before, first'.
items.cn: prior 是 *pri-“在前”的比较级，更早为原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”。

items.en: The sense widens from temporal precedence to rank and ceremonial order.
items.cn: 义项从时间上的在先扩展到等级与礼仪次序。

items.en: Management and administration make priority a countable item: priorities are things to be ranked.
items.cn: 管理与行政把 priority 变成可数事项：priorities 是待排序的东西。

items.en: Modern English also uses priority in computing, traffic law, and diplomacy, wherever a queue needs a rule.
items.cn: 现代英语还把 priority 用于计算机、交通法与外交，凡队列需要规则之处皆可。

note.en: The first group shares the prior stem; the second is about words that also mean precedence or importance.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior 词干，第二组看同样表示“居先”或“重要”的词。

entries.definition: earlier or more important. It is the adjective behind priority.
entries.definitionCN: 更早或更重要的。它是 priority 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: to rank things and act on the first one.
the act of ranking by importance.
the right to go before others, especially in ceremony. It stresses order, not urgency.
entries.definitionCN: 先于他人的权利，尤用于礼仪。它强调次序，而非紧迫。

entries.definition: a liking for one thing over another. It is personal taste, not a ranked obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物胜过另一物的喜爱。它是个人偏好，不是排序义务。

entries.definition: the quality of needing immediate action. It explains why something is a priority.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立即行动的性质。它解释某事为何成为优先。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Medieval Latin prioritas, the prior/priority pair, triage and traffic uses, and the phrases top priority and low priority.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：中世纪拉丁语 prioritas、prior 与 priority 这对词、分诊与交通用法，以及 top priority / low priority 两个短语。

normal.en: Priority is prior plus -ity: it names whatever stands first in the line.
normal.cn: priority 是 prior 加 -ity：它命名排在队伍最前的东西。

normal.en: It can be a thing (a priority) or a status (to have priority). The first is countable, the second is relational.
normal.cn: 它可以是事物（a priority），也可以是状态（to have priority）。前者可数，后者是关系。

normal.en: Triage is priority in action: red tags move first, green tags wait.
normal.cn: 分诊是 priority 的实战：红标先走，绿标等待。

normal.en: Top priority is deliberately redundant; the doubling signals urgency in political speech.
normal.cn: top priority 是刻意冗余；这种重复在政治语言中标记紧迫。

normal.en: Low priority does not mean unimportant: it means postponable, still in the queue.
normal.cn: low priority 不是不重要：它意味着可推迟，仍在队列里。

abstract.en: Priority is scarcity made visible: when time or space is limited, someone must be ranked above someone else.
abstract.cn: 优先是稀缺的可见化：当时间或空间有限，总得有人被排在别人之上。

abstract.en: Every ranking is an argument about values disguised as a schedule.
abstract.cn: 每一种排序都是伪装成日程的价值争论。

abstract.en: The word began as 'earlier' and became 'more important'; modern life quietly assumes the first deserves the second.
abstract.cn: 这个词从“更早”变成“更重要”；现代生活悄悄假定先来的理应优先。

examples.en: The safety of children must take priority over cost.
examples.cn: 儿童安全必须优先于成本。

examples.en: Deciding priorities is the hardest part of the job.
examples.cn: 决定优先次序是这份工作最难的部分。

examples.en: Emergency vehicles have priority at the junction.
examples.cn: 紧急车辆在交叉口有优先通行权。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来奥瑞提”——先扑过来的那一个，奥瑞提先被叫号 → priority 优先、优先事项

root: 中世纪拉丁语 prioritas“优先、居先”，源出拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，再上为 *pri- / PIE *per-“在前”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of priority, all about a queue. The queue can be moral (top priority), legal (the right of way), ceremonial (order of procession), or digital (a process level).
sensesIntro.cn: priority 的九个义项都关于一条队列。这条队列可以是道德的（头等大事）、法律的（通行权）、礼仪的（行列位次）或数字的（进程等级）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ranked queue in which one item is served first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被排序的队列，其中一项先被服务。

branches.en: FIRST CLAIM: one thing is treated as more important, whether named or as a status.
branches.cn: 第一诉求：某物被当作更重要，无论作为事项还是状态。

branches.en: ORDER: several claims are ranked into a list or a ceremonial sequence.
branches.cn: 次序：多项诉求被排成列表或礼仪序列。

branches.en: TRAFFIC: the ranking becomes a right to move first.
branches.cn: 交通：排序变成先行动的权利。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the queue is numeric, and priority decides which task jumps ahead.
branches.cn: 计算机：队列变成数字，优先级决定哪个任务插队。

branches.en: SCALE AND TIME: top and low mark urgency, while the archaic sense keeps the temporal origin.
branches.cn: 尺度与时间：top 与 low 标记紧迫，古义保留时间起源。

intro.en: Priority is a noun from Medieval Latin prioritas. English adds -ize, -ation, and -ed, and the base prior also gives priory and prioress.
intro.cn: priority 是来自中世纪拉丁 prioritas 的名词。英语加 -ize、-ation、-ed，词基 prior 还生成 priory 与 prioress。

latinIntro.en: Latin prior 'former' and prioritas 'precedence' sit beside primus 'first'. The family ranks things along a line from earlier to more important.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者”与 prioritas“居先”旁边是 primus“第一”。这个词族沿一条从“更早”到“更重要”的线给事物排序。

items.meaning: to treat one thing as more important than others
items.meaningCN: 优先处理（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: the act of ranking by importance
ranked and treated as most important
a monastery headed by a prior
a female superior of a priory

items.meaningCN: 居先；位次优先（近义同族）

definition_zh: 本质上；基本上；实际上
definition_en: in the most basic and important way
core_image: 剥掉层层外壳，露出最里面的核
scene: 这两种方案本质上是一样的，只是说法不同。 The two plans are essentially the same, just described in different words.
sceneCN: 这里 essentially 是「本质上」（第 1 个义项：就最根本的性质而言）；句意：这两种方案本质上是一样的，只是说法不同。

senses.title: In basic nature
senses.definition: in the most basic and important way
senses.definitionCN: 就最根本、最重要的方面而言
senses.example: The two theories are essentially the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种理论本质上相同。
senses.why: The adverb strips away surface differences to show the inner nature.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词剥去表面差异，露出内在本质。

senses.title: In practice
senses.definition: used to say what something really amounts to
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事物实际上等于什么
senses.example: The job is essentially about listening to people.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作实际上就是倾听人们说话。
senses.why: Saying what something really is brings the idea down to its effect.
senses.whyCN: 说明某事物究竟是什么，就是把概念落到实际效果上。

intro.en: Essentially is essential plus -ly, from Latin essentia, being.
intro.cn: essentially 由 essential 加 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 essentia（存在）。

items.en: Essentia means being or nature.
items.cn: essentia 意为存在或本性。

items.en: Essentialis means of the essence.
items.cn: essentialis 意为属于本质的。

items.en: Essential enters English as an adjective.
items.cn: essential 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly forms essentially.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成 essentially。

items.en: The adverb softens a claim to its core truth.
items.cn: 这个副词把断言收拢到核心真实。

note.en: Essentially is close to basically and fundamentally.
note.cn: essentially 与 basically、fundamentally 相近。

entries.definition: completely necessary
basic nature
belief in fixed natures
in the main or most basic way
in a basic and important way
in practice, almost the same as

normalIntro.en: Essentially points to the kernel under the shell of details.
normalIntro.cn: essentially 指向细节外壳下的那个核。

normal.en: Essentially the same means different in details only.
normal.cn: essentially the same 意为只是细节不同。

normal.en: Essentially unchanged means no real change happened.
normal.cn: essentially unchanged 意为没有真正改变。

normal.en: Essentially correct means right in the main points.
normal.cn: essentially correct 意为主要方面正确。

normal.en: The word often softens a strong claim.
normal.cn: 这个词常用来缓和强烈的断言。

normal.en: Compare basically: basically is looser, essentially points to essence.
normal.cn: 对比 basically：basically 更宽松，essentially 指向本质。

abstract.en: Picture peeling an onion down to its center.
abstract.cn: 想象把洋葱一层层剥到中心。

abstract.en: Imagine two roads that meet at the same point.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路最终汇到同一点。

abstract.en: Think of two cups of different shape holding the same tea.
abstract.cn: 想象两只形状不同的杯子装着同样的茶。

examples.en: The two designs are essentially the same.
examples.cn: 这两个设计本质上相同。

examples.en: Her answer was essentially correct.
examples.cn: 她的回答基本上是正确的。

examples.en: The problem is essentially one of trust.
examples.cn: 这个问题本质上是信任问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essential（本质的）＋ ly」——从本质上来看，就是「基本上」；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 essentia（存在、本性）→ essential（本质的）＋ -ly → essentially，核心义「从最根本的性质看」。

sensesIntro.en: Essentially first points to basic nature, and then to what something really amounts to in practice.
sensesIntro.cn: essentially 先指向基本性质，再指向事物在实际中究竟等于什么。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the kernel left after every outer layer is removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：剥掉所有外层后剩下的核。

branches.en: The first sense looks at the inner nature.
branches.cn: 首要义项看的是内在性质。

branches.en: The second sense says what a thing really is.
branches.cn: 第二个义项说明事物实际上是什么。

branches.en: What something really is follows from its nature.
branches.cn: 事物实际上是什么，由其本性决定。

branches.en: The adverb often reduces surface differences.
branches.cn: 这个副词常用来消解表面差异。

branches.en: It also softens a claim to its main truth.
branches.cn: 它也把断言缓和到主要真实。

intro.en: Essentially is essential plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: essentially 是 essential 加副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Essentia, being, underlies essential and essentially.
latinIntro.cn: essentia（存在）是 essential 与 essentially 的根基。

items.example: Esse gives the idea of being.

definition_zh: 金融；财政；资金；为……提供资金
definition_en: the management of money, public revenue, the money needed for a project, or to provide money for something
core_image: 账本上一列数字被红笔圈出，旁边写着收支平衡
scene: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。 The company needs finance to expand production.
sceneCN: 这里 finance 是「资金」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。

senses.title: Money management
senses.definition: the management of money and investment
senses.definitionCN: 对货币与投资的管理
senses.example: She works in finance.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事金融工作。
senses.why: This is the broad field sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是广义领域义。

senses.title: Public revenue
senses.definition: the money and spending of a government
senses.definitionCN: 政府的收入与支出
senses.example: Public finance pays for roads and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 公共财政支付道路与学校。
senses.why: The field sense narrows to government.
senses.whyCN: 领域义缩小到政府。

senses.title: Funds
senses.definition: the money needed for a project
senses.definitionCN: 项目所需的钱
senses.example: The company needs finance to expand production.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。
senses.why: Money for a purpose is finance.
senses.whyCN: 为某个目的准备的钱就是资金。

senses.title: To fund
senses.definition: to provide money for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供资金
senses.example: The city financed the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府为新桥提供资金。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of providing money.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为提供资金的动作。

intro.en: Finance comes from Middle French finance, a settlement of debt, from finer, to settle, from Latin finis, end.
intro.cn: finance 出自中古法语 finance（清偿债务），源于 finer（了结），再追溯到拉丁语 finis（终点）。

items.en: Finis meant end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Finer meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finer 意为了结债务。

items.en: Finance named the settling of money matters.
items.cn: finance 指钱财事务的了结。

items.en: Finance named the management of money.
items.cn: finance 指对金钱的管理。

items.en: It also became a verb meaning to fund.
items.cn: 它也变成动词，意为提供资金。

note.en: Finance is compared with similar-looking words and with words for money matters.
note.cn: 把 finance 与形近词以及表示钱财事务的词作比较。

entries.definition: relating to money
a person who manages large sums
a sum paid as punishment
money provided for a purpose
coins and notes used to pay
the business of banks

normalIntro.en: Finance is money managed, money raised, and money provided.
normalIntro.cn: finance 是被管理的钱、被筹集的资金与被提供的款项。

normal.en: Finance began with settling debts.
normal.cn: finance 最初与了结债务有关。

normal.en: Public finance belongs to the state.
normal.cn: 公共财政属于国家。

normal.en: A project needs finance to start.
normal.cn: 项目需要资金才能启动。

normal.en: To finance is to pay for something.
normal.cn: to finance 意为为某事出钱。

normal.en: The adjective is financial.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 financial。

abstract.en: Money is stored effort, moved from hand to hand.
abstract.cn: 钱是储存起来的劳动，从一只手流到另一只手。

abstract.en: A budget is a promise about the future.
abstract.cn: 预算是一份关于未来的承诺。

abstract.en: What a society funds shows what it values.
abstract.cn: 一个社会资助什么，就显示它重视什么。

examples.en: The company needs finance to expand production.
examples.cn: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。

examples.en: She works in finance.
examples.cn: 她从事金融工作。

examples.en: The city financed the new bridge.
examples.cn: 市政府为新桥提供资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: finance 出自中古法语 finance（清偿债务），源于 finer（了结），本义「结清钱款」，后指金融、财政、资金与提供资金。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（终点）经法语 finer（了结），核心义「了结钱款、管理钱财」。

sensesIntro.en: Finance means money management, public revenue, project funds, or to provide money.
sensesIntro.cn: finance 意为金融、财政、资金或提供资金。

core.en: Money brought under control and put to use.
core.cn: 被管理并投入使用的金钱。

branches.en: The field that manages money.
branches.cn: 管理金钱的领域。

branches.en: The state's income and spending.
branches.cn: 国家的收入与支出。

branches.en: Money gathered for a purpose.
branches.cn: 为某个目的筹集的资金。

branches.en: The act of paying for something.
branches.cn: 为某事付款的动作。

branches.en: The field and the funds share one name.
branches.cn: 领域与资金共用一个名称。

intro.en: Finance belongs to the Latin finis family of settling and ending.
intro.cn: finance 属于拉丁语 finis（终点）词族，关联了结与结算。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis and French finer are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与法语 finer 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 一家银行为这笔交易提供资金。

items.example: The financial year ends in March.

items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了这个项目。

definition_zh: 不快乐的；不幸福的；不满意的；不幸的
definition_en: sad, dissatisfied, or not well suited to a situation
core_image: 生日蛋糕前的蜡烛烧了半天，脸上却提不起笑
scene: 搬进新家的第一个晚上，孩子在陌生的床上翻来覆去，说想回去。 She was unhappy in the new town.
sceneCN: 这里 unhappy 是「不快乐的」（第 1 个义项：心情不悦）；句意为她在那座新城里过得不开心。烛光里提不起笑的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不快乐地；不幸地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不快乐；不幸」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「快乐的」
肯定形式的名词，义为「幸福」

senses.title: Sad in mood
senses.definition: feeling sad or low over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里感到难过、情绪低落
senses.example: He was unhappy for weeks after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家后的几个星期他一直不高兴。
senses.why: The prefix denies happy, and happy itself came from hap, meaning chance or good luck.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 happy，而 happy 本出自 hap（机遇、好运），于是不快乐就是没有好运相伴。

senses.title: Not satisfied with something
senses.definition: displeased with a decision, a service, or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某个决定、服务或状况感到不满
senses.example: Many parents were unhappy about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家长对新课表不满。
senses.why: To be without good luck is to be without what you wanted, which reads as complaint.
senses.whyCN: 没有好运也就没有所求之物，这份欠缺读起来就是不满。

senses.title: A period or relationship without joy
senses.definition: used of times or relationships that contain more sorrow than joy
senses.definitionCN: 形容包含更多悲伤而少有欢乐的时期或关系
senses.example: It was an unhappy marriage from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 那段婚姻从一开始就不幸福。
senses.why: A stretch of life inherits the feeling of the people living it.
senses.whyCN: 一段时光会继承生活在其中的人的感受。

senses.title: Unlucky in its timing or outcome
senses.definition: used of an event that turns out badly or comes at a bad moment
senses.definitionCN: 形容结果不好或发生得不巧的事
senses.example: It was an unhappy coincidence that both letters arrived the same day.
senses.exampleCN: 两封信同一天到，真是不巧的巧合。
senses.why: The old sense of hap as chance explains why unhappy can still mean unlucky.
senses.whyCN: hap 原本就是「机遇」，这解释了为什么 unhappy 至今还能表示「不巧」。

senses.title: Not appropriate or happy in choice
senses.definition: used of a word or choice that is unfortunate rather than wrong
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个词或选择不恰当，而不是错误
senses.example: An unhappy phrase made the report sound cold.
senses.exampleCN: 一个失当的措辞让报告听起来冷冰冰。
senses.why: Happy once meant fitting or apt, so an unhappy phrase is one that does not fit.
senses.whyCN: happy 曾经也有「恰当、合宜」之义，因此 unhappy phrase 指不合适的说法。

intro.en: Happy comes from the old noun hap, chance, and the negative prefix was added in English.
intro.cn: happy 来自古词 hap（机遇），否定前缀是英语自己加上去的。

items.en: Happ meant chance or luck, and English took the noun early.
items.cn: happ 意为机遇、运气，英语很早就借入了这个名词。

items.en: Happy first meant lucky or favoured by chance.
items.cn: happy 最初意为「幸运的、得其时运」。

items.en: The sense shifted from good luck to good feeling.
items.cn: 其义由「好运」转向「好心情」。

items.en: Unhappy is recorded from the seventeenth century for sadness and displeasure.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，unhappy 有悲伤与不满的用法记录。

items.en: The older sense of unlucky survives in phrases about coincidences.
items.cn: 较古的「不巧」之义仍存于讲巧合的说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the happy family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for sadness.
note.cn: 形近组是 happy 词族，近义组汇集表示悲伤的词。

entries.definition: glad and content
in a sad way
the state of being sad
awkward to use
entries.definitionCN: 不便使用的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: extremely unhappy
feeling sorrow
not pleased with something
glad and content

normalIntro.en: The word denies an old word for luck, which is why sadness and bad timing share one form.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定了古老的「运气」一词，所以悲伤与不巧共用同一形态。

normal.en: Un- plus happy: not favoured by luck.
normal.cn: un- 加 happy：没被运气眷顾。

normal.en: Be unhappy about is the usual pattern for complaints.
normal.cn: be unhappy about 是表达不满的常见搭配。

normal.en: Perhaps and happen come from the same hap root.
normal.cn: perhaps 与 happen 同出 hap 这个词根。

normal.en: Unhappier and unhappiest change the y to i before the endings.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级要把 y 变成 i 再加词尾。

normal.en: Unhappiness is the noun, and it is uncountable.
normal.cn: unhappiness 是名词，且不可数。

abstract.en: Picture a child sitting on an unmade bed in a new room.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子坐在新房间里没铺好的床上。

abstract.en: See candles burning down over an untouched cake.
abstract.cn: 看蜡烛烧下去，蛋糕却没人动。

abstract.en: Hear a laugh that stops a moment too early.
abstract.cn: 听一声笑得早了半拍就停下的笑。

examples.en: The children were unhappy about leaving their old school.
examples.cn: 孩子们对离开原来的学校很不高兴。

examples.en: She had an unhappy year before the family moved.
examples.cn: 搬家前那一年她过得很不快乐。

examples.en: He smiled unhappily and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他不快地笑了笑，什么也没说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺哈皮」——俺以为会哈皮一整天，结果一个人待着，怎么也乐不起来。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ happy，happy 源自古诺斯语 happ（机遇、运气），中世纪由「好运」转义为「快乐」

sensesIntro.en: One denied luck covers a sad mood, a complaint, a joyless time, and a clumsy phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份被否定的运气，覆盖低落的心情、抱怨、无乐的时光与失当的措辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: candles burning down in front of a face that cannot smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：蜡烛烧着，脸上却笑不起来。

branches.en: The mood branch: a long stretch of low feeling.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：一段漫长的低落。

branches.en: The complaint branch: disappointment with a decision.
branches.cn: 抱怨分支：对某个决定的不满。

branches.en: The relationship branch: years with more sorrow than joy.
branches.cn: 关系分支：悲多于喜的年月。

branches.en: The chance branch: the old sense of an unlucky turn.
branches.cn: 机缘分支：运气不佳的古老义。

branches.en: The wording branch: a phrase that does not fit.
branches.cn: 措辞分支：不合宜的说法。

definition_zh: 购买；购置；购得之物；（以努力或牺牲）取得；紧握；抓握力；杠杆支点；（古）掠夺所得
definition_en: to get something by paying money, or to obtain it by effort; also the firm hold by which power is applied
core_image: 一个人向前追着猎物跑，追上后死死攥住不放——先「追着取得」，很久以后才专指「用钱买下」
scene: 五金店的经理敲着盒子提醒顾客保留小票。 This purchase over fifty dollars cannot be returned without a receipt.
sceneCN: 这里 purchase 是「购得之物」（第 3 个义项：已经买到手的东西）；句意：留好小票，这件超过五十美元的购得之物没有它就不能退。画面里有柜台、收据和盖章的手；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 购买；购置；（以努力）取得；紧握
购买；购得之物；紧握（力）；杠杆支点

senses.title: To buy: hand over money and take the thing
senses.definition: to get goods, services, or property by paying money for them
senses.definitionCN: 用钱取得货物、服务或财产
senses.example: She purchased a used car for three thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 她花三千美元买了一辆二手车。
senses.why: The verb came from Old French porchacier, pur- 'forth' plus chacier 'to chase': to purchase was to go after something until you had it. Only in the mid-14c. did 'get by paying money' become the dominant sense.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自古法语 porchacier，由 pur-「向前」加 chacier「追逐」构成：purchase 本是「追着去取得」。到 14 世纪中期，「付钱取得」才成为主义。

senses.title: Procurement: the formal act of acquiring
senses.titleCN: 购置：有手续的正式取得
senses.definition: the formal or large-scale act of buying goods, equipment, or property
senses.definitionCN: 正式或大宗地购买货物、设备或财产的行为
senses.example: The university approved the purchase of new laboratory equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 校方批准了购置新的实验室设备。
senses.why: The noun's sense 'act of acquiring, procurement' is recorded from the late 14c. Modern institutions narrowed it to documented buying: the chase is gone, and what remains is a deliberate, recorded acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 名词「取得、采购的行为」记录于 14 世纪后期。现代机构把它收窄为有单据的购买：追逐不见了，剩下的是有步骤、有记录的取得。

senses.title: The thing bought: an object with a receipt
senses.titleCN: 购得之物：带小票的那件东西
senses.definition: something that has been bought
senses.definitionCN: 已经买到手的东西
senses.example: Her most expensive purchase was a second-hand piano.
senses.exampleCN: 她最贵的一件购得之物是一架二手钢琴。
senses.why: 'That which is bought' dates from the 1580s, three centuries after the verb. The older noun meant 'acquisition, booty'; once buying became the main sense, the object bought could inherit the name.
senses.whyCN: 「买到的东西」这一义项始于 16 世纪 80 年代，比动词晚三百年。早先名词指「获得物、战利品」；当购买成为主义，被买下的东西就继承了这个词。

senses.title: To win at a price: obtain by effort or loss
senses.titleCN: 以代价取得：用努力或牺牲换来
senses.definition: to obtain something valuable through effort, suffering, or sacrifice rather than money
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力、受苦或牺牲而得到有价值的东西，而非用钱
senses.example: They purchased their freedom with years of struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用多年的斗争换来了自由。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense: c.1300 purchase meant 'acquire, obtain, procure' by any means, including merit or suffering. 'To purchase peace with blood' keeps that breadth, where money is only one possible price.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项：约 1300 年 purchase 指以任何方式「取得、获得、谋得」，包括功劳或受苦。「以鲜血换取和平」保留了这种宽度，钱只是众多代价之一。

senses.title: A firm grip: the hold that keeps the thing
senses.titleCN: 紧握：攥住不放的那只手
senses.definition: a firm hold or grasp on something, especially one that gives control
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的牢固抓握，尤指带来控制权的握持
senses.example: He got a purchase on the rope and pulled himself up.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住绳子，把自己拉了上去。
senses.why: The noun sense 'firm hold by which power may be exerted' is from 1711, extended from a nautical verb of the 1560s meaning 'to haul or draw, especially by mechanical power', as sailors purchase an anchor. Gripping and buying share the image of pulling something into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 名词「可以施加力量的牢固把握」始于 1711 年，来自 16 世纪 60 年代一个航海动词「拉、绞（尤用机械力）」，如水手绞起锚。抓握与购买共享同一个意象：把东西拉进自己的掌控。

senses.title: Leverage: the point where a small force wins
senses.titleCN: 杠杆支点：小力撬动大物的那个点
senses.definition: a position or hold that gives mechanical advantage, the point where a lever or force bites
senses.definitionCN: 带来机械优势的位置或着力点，即杠杆或力量咬住的那一点
senses.example: Put the jack under the beam to get a better purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 把千斤顶放到梁下，好取得更好的着力点。
senses.why: Mechanical 'purchase' names the hold or position that lets a small force move a great weight, the same word sailors used for hauling. The point where the lever bites is literally a place to grip.
senses.whyCN: 机械上的 purchase 指让小力移动重物的着力点或握位，正是水手「绞拉」时用的词。杠杆咬住的那一点，字面上就是一个可以握紧的地方。

senses.title: Purchasing: buying turned into a department
senses.titleCN: 采购：变成一门部门工作的购买
senses.definition: the institutional activity or department responsible for buying supplies and equipment
senses.definitionCN: 负责购买物资与设备的机构性活动或部门
senses.example: She works in purchasing, sourcing parts for the whole factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她在采购部工作，为整个工厂寻找零件。
senses.why: In business and government, purchasing became a department and a process in the 20th c.: purchase orders, purchasing agents. The act of buying is institutionalised and separated from the person who pays.
senses.whyCN: 在商业与政府里，purchasing 在 20 世纪成为一个部门和流程：采购订单、采购员。购买行为被制度化，与掏钱的人分开了。

senses.title: To secure title: land and rights, not shopping
senses.titleCN: 置产、买断：买的是产权，不是商品
senses.definition: to acquire property, land, or legal rights by payment, especially on a large or formal scale
senses.definitionCN: 通过付款取得财产、土地或法律权利，尤指大宗或正式的
senses.example: The company purchased the land from the county in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司于 1998 年从县政府买下了这块土地。
senses.why: Legal and landed use keeps the noun's weight: a purchase of land or of rights is an acquisition of title, not a shopping trip. The word still carries the old sense of getting something permanently into your holdings.
senses.whyCN: 法律与地产用法保留了名词的分量：purchase of land or rights 是取得产权，而不是逛街购物。这个词仍带着「把某物永久纳入自己名下」的旧义。

senses.title: Booty: what was taken before it was bought
senses.titleCN: 掠夺所得：还没「买」之前，是抢来的
senses.definition: in older usage, goods gained by pillage or robbery; spoils
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法：通过掠夺或抢劫得到的财物；战利品
senses.example: In the old chronicle, the raiders divided their purchase among the ships.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，劫掠者把抢来的财物分给了各条船。
senses.why: The noun's first English sense (c.1300) was 'booty, spoil, goods gained by pillage'; 'to make purchase' once meant 'to seize by robbery'. The polite buyer of today stands where a raider once stood.
senses.whyCN: 名词最早的英语义项（约 1300 年）是「战利品、掠夺所得」；to make purchase 一度意为「抢劫夺取」。今天彬彬有礼的买主，站的是当年劫掠者的位置。

intro.en: Purchase begins as a chase, not a transaction: Old French porchacier meant to go after something and get it. Money entered the word only in the 14th century, and the grip-and-lever senses came from sailors hauling anchors.
intro.cn: purchase 起于追逐而非交易：古法语 porchacier 意为追着去取得。金钱在 14 世纪才进入这个词，而「抓握、杠杆」义来自水手绞锚。

items.en: Porchacier (later pourchasser) meant 'search for, procure; aim at, strive for, pursue eagerly'. It joins pur- 'forth' with chacier 'to run after, hunt, chase' (see chase). The exact force of pur- here, whether 'forward' or an intensive, is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: Porchacier（后作 pourchasser）意为「寻找、谋得、力求、急切追求」，由 pur-「向前」加 chacier「追赶、打猎、追逐」（见 chase）构成。pur- 在此究竟是「向前」还是加强语气，来源不确定，故标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: The Anglo-French verb purchaser meant 'go after' and carried the legal-administrative tone of obtaining something. English took it over as purchase with a very wide meaning.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语动词 purchaser 意为「追赶、追求」，并带有取得某物的法律行政语气。英语借用为 purchase，含义非常宽。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as 'acquire, obtain; get, receive; procure, provide', also 'bring about, instigate, contrive'. At this stage money is not required: merit, suffering, or effort can be the price.
items.cn: 动词最早记录为「取得、获得、得到、领受、谋得、提供」，也有「促成、煽动、策划」义。此时并不需要金钱：功劳、受苦或努力都可以是代价。

items.en: The specific sense 'acquire or secure by expenditure of money or its equivalent, pay money for, buy' appears in the mid-14c. The older 'get by conquest in war, obtain as booty' survived into the 17c.
items.cn: 「以金钱或其等价物取得、付钱买下」这一具体义项出现于 14 世纪中期。更早的「以战争征服取得、作为战利品获得」一直用到 17 世纪。

items.en: A nautical verb 'to haul or draw, especially by mechanical power' (1560s, used of hauling up anchors) produced the noun sense 'firm hold by which power may be exerted' in 1711. Meanwhile 'that which is bought' is recorded from the 1580s.
items.cn: 航海动词「拉、绞，尤指用机械力」（16 世纪 60 年代，用于绞起锚）在 1711 年衍生出名词「可以施加力量的牢固把握」；同时「买到的东西」记录于 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: The noun's journey runs from 'booty, spoil' (c.1300) to 'act of acquiring' (late 14c.) to 'thing bought' (1580s) and finally to the 20th-century department of purchasing. Plunder, transaction, object, institution: one word, four stages.
items.cn: 名词的旅程从「战利品、掠夺物」（约 1300）到「取得行为」（14 世纪后期），再到「买到的东西」（16 世纪 80 年代），最后到 20 世纪的采购部门。劫掠、交易、物品、机构：一个词，四个阶段。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to follow or chase someone, or to work toward a goal. It echoes purchase in sound but comes from Latin prosequi, not from chacier.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追求。它与 purchase 读音相近，但来自拉丁语 prosequi，而非 chacier。

entries.definition: the act of chasing or striving for something. Like pursue, it belongs to the sequi 'follow' family.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追求。与 pursue 一样属于 sequi「跟随」词族。

entries.definition: to read through carefully. It looks like purchase but has no etymological link.
entries.definitionCN: 细读；浏览。它形似 purchase，但词源上毫无关联。

entries.definition: an aim or intention. It also begins with pur-, but the second element is poser 'to place'.
entries.definitionCN: 目的；意图。它同样以 pur- 开头，但后半是 poser「放置」。

entries.definition: to get something by paying money. It is the short native verb where purchase is the formal one.
entries.definitionCN: 买。它是简短的本族动词，purchase 则是正式用词。

entries.definition: to come to possess something, often through effort or over time, not necessarily by payment.
entries.definitionCN: 获得；取得。常指通过努力或随时间而拥有，不一定付钱。

entries.definition: to obtain something, especially with care or difficulty. It matches the oldest sense of purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 设法取得，尤指费心或费力地。它对应 purchase 最古老的义项。

entries.definition: to get something, especially by request or effort. Neutral in tone, wider than buy.
entries.definitionCN: 获得。尤指通过请求或努力，语气中性，比 buy 宽。

entries.definition: a firm hold on something. It covers the physical sense of purchase as grip or leverage.
entries.definitionCN: 紧握；抓握。它对应 purchase 表示抓握或着力点的实指义。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Old French chacier 'to chase', Anglo-French purchaser, and the nautical hauling sense that gave us the grip.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：古法语 chacier「追逐」、盎格鲁-法语 purchaser，以及带来「抓握」义的航海绞拉用法。

normal.en: purchase = pur- 'forward' + chase: you chase something forward until it is yours.
normal.cn: purchase = pur-「向前」+ chase「追」：你一路往前追，直到它归你所有。

normal.en: The same chase lives in catch and capture: to purchase is to run something down and seize it.
normal.cn: 同一个 chase 也活在 catch 和 capture 里：purchase 就是把东西追到手并抓住。

normal.en: Sailors purchase an anchor by hauling it up; that is why a good foothold is also called a purchase.
normal.cn: 水手用绞拉的方式 purchase（绞起）锚；所以一个稳的落脚点也叫 purchase（着力点）。

normal.en: A purchaser is simply the person at the end of the chase, holding the receipt.
normal.cn: purchaser 不过是追逐终点的那个拿着小票的人。

normal.en: To purchase peace with blood is the word's oldest logic: the price need not be money.
normal.cn: 以鲜血 purchase 和平，是这个词最古老的逻辑：代价不必是钱。

abstract.en: The core is possession by pursuit: first you chase, then you hold, and only later do you pay.
abstract.cn: 核心是「追而得之」：先追、再抓，最后才付钱。

abstract.en: Money is a late guest in this word, not its host.
abstract.cn: 金钱在这个词里是迟到的客人，而不是主人。

abstract.en: Purchase keeps a raider and a shopper in one body: booty, then bargain.
abstract.cn: purchase 把劫掠者和购物者装在同一个身体里：先是战利品，后是讨价还价。

examples.en: The city purchased the old railway yard and turned it into a park.
examples.cn: 市政府买下了旧铁路场，把它改造成了公园。

examples.en: Keep your receipt as proof of purchase in case the radio fails.
examples.cn: 留好小票作为购买凭证，以防收音机出故障。

examples.en: The climber finally got a purchase on the rock and pulled himself over the edge.
examples.cn: 攀登者终于抓牢了岩壁，把自己拉上了边缘。

dict_mnemonic.text: pur（向前）+ chase（追）——追上去一把抓住，后来才变成「花钱买下」→ purchase 购买

root: 源自拉丁语系：古法语 porchacier（pur-「向前」+ chacier「追逐」，同 chase）经盎格鲁-法语 purchaser 进入英语，本义「追着取得」，14 世纪中期才特化为「用钱买」；「抓握、着力点」义另出自 16 世纪水手绞锚的航海动词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one arc: chase, seize, pay, own. The verb starts as 'get by going after', narrows to 'buy', then splits into the object bought, the grip that holds it, the lever point that moves it, and the institution that orders it.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着一条弧线：追、抓、付、拥有。动词从「追着取得」开始，收窄为「买」，再分出「买到的东西」「攥住它的手」「撬动它的支点」以及「下订单的机构」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chasing something down and closing your hand around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：追着一样东西跑，最后把它攥进手心。

branches.en: THE TRANSACTION: ordinary buying, and the formal act of procurement.
branches.cn: 交易：日常购买，以及正式的购置行为。

branches.en: WHAT IS TAKEN: the thing bought, and the old booty seized by force.
branches.cn: 被取走之物：买到的东西，以及旧时武力夺来的战利品。

branches.en: GETTING BY OTHER MEANS: winning through sacrifice, and securing property by title.
branches.cn: 以别的代价取得：用牺牲换来，以及以产权买断。

branches.en: THE GRIP: a firm hold, and the point where a lever bites.
branches.cn: 抓握：牢固的握持，以及杠杆咬住的着力点。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: purchasing as a department, an order, a process.
branches.cn: 机构：作为部门、订单与流程的采购。

intro.en: Purchase is pur- plus chacier plus the English noun ending. Its family shows the prefix pur- 'forth', the root chac-/capt- 'to chase, seize', and the suffixes -er, -ing, -able, and re-.
intro.cn: purchase 是 pur- 加 chacier，再加英语名词词尾。它的词族展示前缀 pur-「向前」、词根 chac-/capt-「追逐、抓取」，以及后缀 -er、-ing、-able 和 re-。

latinIntro.en: Behind chacier stands Vulgar Latin captiare and Latin captare 'to try to catch', from capere 'to take'. The same capere yields capture, captive and catch, so buying and seizing are cousins.
latinIntro.cn: chacier 背后是通俗拉丁语 captiare 与拉丁语 captare「设法抓住」，源自 capere「拿取」。同一个 capere 还给出 capture、captive、catch，因此「买」与「抓」是表亲。

items.meaning: to obtain by chasing, then by paying
items.example: They purchased the house in cash.
items.exampleCN: 他们用现金买下了这栋房子。

items.meaningCN: 购买者；买主（-er 施事后缀）
items.example: The purchaser must be over eighteen.
items.exampleCN: 购买者必须年满十八岁。

items.meaning: the act or department of buying
to buy back or buy again
items.example: The firm repurchased two million shares.
items.exampleCN: 该公司回购了两百万股。

items.meaningCN: 可购得的（-able 形容词后缀）

items.meaning: to run after in order to catch
items.meaningCN: 追逐；追赶（purchase 的后半身）
items.example: The dog chased the ball across the lawn.

items.meaningCN: 抓住；接住（chase 的同源双式词）
items.example: He caught the falling cup just in time.
items.exampleCN: 他及时接住了掉下来的杯子。

items.meaning: to take by force; the act of taking
items.meaningCN: 俘获；夺取（capere 的另一支后裔）
items.example: The soldiers captured the bridge at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明夺取了那座桥。

items.example: The unpurchased land stayed wild for decades.
items.exampleCN: 那块未被买下的土地荒了几十年。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 追赶；打猎（chacier 的直接来源）

definition_zh: 现金；现款；兑现；赚钱
definition_en: money in the form of coins and notes, or to exchange a cheque for money
core_image: 钱箱里随时能拿出来的现钱
scene: 结账时收银员问怎么付款。 She paid in cash and put the receipt in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 cash 指「现金」（第 1 个义项：硬币和纸币形式的钱）；句意是她付了现金，把收据放进包里。

senses.title: Money in coins and notes
senses.definition: money in the form of coins and banknotes rather than cheques or cards
senses.definitionCN: 以硬币和纸币形式存在的钱，而非支票或银行卡
senses.example: He always carries some cash for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他总带些现金坐公交。
senses.why: The Latin source meant a money box, and the word shifted from the box to the ready money kept inside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是钱箱，词义从箱子转到箱子里随时可取的现钱。

senses.title: To exchange a cheque for money
senses.definition: to give or receive coins and notes in exchange for a cheque or other paper
senses.definitionCN: 用支票或其他票据换取硬币和纸币
senses.example: She cashed her salary cheque at the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行把工资支票兑成了现金。
senses.why: If cash is ready money, the verb names the act of turning paper into that ready money.
senses.whyCN: 既然 cash 是现钱，动词就指把票据变成现钱的动作。

senses.title: Funds available to a business
senses.definition: money that a company or person has available to spend at once
senses.definitionCN: 公司或个人当下可以动用的钱
senses.example: The firm ran out of cash in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在春天耗尽了资金。
senses.why: For a business, ready money on hand becomes a measure of health, so cash stands for available funds.
senses.whyCN: 对企业而言，手头的现钱成了经营健康的尺度，于是 cash 代指可动用资金。

intro.en: Cash goes back to a Latin word for a box, then to the money box and finally to the money inside.
intro.cn: cash 可追到拉丁语表示盒子的词，再经钱箱义，最后指箱子里的钱。

items.en: Capsa was a box or case, the container that held valuables.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 指盒子或箱子，用来盛放贵重物品。

items.en: Italian cassa named a chest or money box in banking and trade.
items.cn: 意大利语 cassa 在金融和贸易中指钱柜或钱箱。

items.en: Middle French casse carried the money-box sense into northern Europe.
items.cn: 中古法语 casse 把钱箱义带到了北欧。

items.en: English cash first names a money box and soon the coin kept in it.
items.cn: 英语 cash 先指钱箱，很快又指箱里存放的硬币。

items.en: Banking adds the verb sense of cashing a cheque and the phrase cash flow.
items.cn: 银行业务又添上兑现支票的动词义和现金流这一说法。

note.en: The first group shares the money-box root, the second lists other words for money and payment.
note.cn: 第一组共享钱箱这一词根，第二组列出其他表示钱与支付的词。

entries.definition: a person who takes and pays out money
working without coins or notes
a record of money received and paid
the money used in a country
a piece of metal money
an amount paid or the act of paying
entries.definitionCN: 支付的款项或付款行为

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the money-box root, the fixed banking phrases and the short verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用钱箱词根、固定银行搭配，以及简短的动词形式。

normal.en: Cash and case share a Latin root meaning box, so cash is literally the money in the box.
normal.cn: cash 与 case 共享表示盒子的拉丁词根，cash 字面上就是箱子里的钱。

normal.en: A cashier is the person at the box, the one who takes and gives money.
normal.cn: cashier 就是守着钱箱的人，负责收钱和付钱。

normal.en: Cash flow pictures money moving in and out like water through a pipe.
normal.cn: cash flow 把钱的进出想象成水流过管道。

normal.en: Pay in cash is the everyday phrase that keeps the noun sense alive.
normal.cn: pay in cash 是让名词义保持活跃的日常说法。

normal.en: The third person cashes and the past cashed both keep the short -sh stem.
normal.cn: 三单 cashes 和过去式 cashed 都保留了短短的 -sh 词干。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden box overflowing with coins on a shop counter.
abstract.cn: 想象商店柜台上一个装满硬币的木箱。

abstract.en: Picture notes folded into a wallet before a trip.
abstract.cn: 想象出门前把纸币折好塞进钱包。

abstract.en: Picture a cheque turning into a stack of notes at the bank window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张支票在银行窗口变成一叠钞票。

examples.en: I have no cash with me today.
examples.cn: 我今天身上没带现金。

examples.en: Can you cash this cheque for me?
examples.cn: 你能帮我兑现这张支票吗？

examples.en: The shop only accepts cash.
examples.cn: 这家店只收现金。

dict_mnemonic.text: cash 读音接近「喀什」：想象在喀什的集市上掏出现金买东西。

root: 源自拉丁语 capsa（盒），经意大利语 cassa、中古法语 casse 进入英语，本指钱箱，后指箱中的现钱。

sensesIntro.en: A money box gives the ready money inside it, then the act of turning paper into that money, then the funds a business holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 钱箱先给出箱里的现钱，再给出把票据换成现钱的动作，最后给出企业持有的资金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box of ready money kept close at hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着现钱、随手可取的钱箱。

branches.en: The notes and coins in the box become the everyday cash sense.
branches.cn: 箱里的纸币和硬币成了日常的现金义。

branches.en: The verb turns a cheque into the contents of the box.
branches.cn: 动词义把支票变成箱子里的东西。

branches.en: For a company the box stands for the funds it can spend now.
branches.cn: 对公司来说，这只箱子代表它眼下能动用的资金。

branches.en: Both senses turn on the same contrast between paper claims and real money.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕票据与真钱之间的同一对照。

branches.en: Ready money is both what you carry and what a business measures.
branches.cn: 现钱既是随身携带的钱，也是企业衡量的指标。

intro.en: Cash grows a compact family through the -ier and -less endings and a few compounds.
intro.cn: cash 通过 -ier、-less 词尾和少量复合词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The ultimate source is Latin capsa, a box, which also underlies case and capsule.
latinIntro.cn: 最终源头是拉丁语 capsa（盒子），case 与 capsule 也出自这里。

items.example: Cash is king in small shops.

items.meaning: he or she exchanges for money
items.example: She cashes her cheque on Fridays.
He cashed the cheque at noon.
Cashing a cheque takes a minute.
The cashier counted the notes twice.
items.exampleCN: 收银员把钞票数了两遍。

items.example: The city is almost cashless now.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市如今几乎不用现金。

items.meaning: a book recording money paid and received
items.example: Every entry goes into the cashbook.

items.meaning: the movement of money in and out
items.exampleCN: 出售之后现金流好转了。

latinEntries.example: Capsa is the deep source of cash.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cash 的深层来源。

latinEntries.example: Cassa named the chest in old banks.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cassa 在老式银行里指钱柜。

definition_zh: 货车；厢式车；面包车；（英）火车行李车厢
definition_en: a covered vehicle for carrying goods or people, smaller than a lorry and closed at the back
core_image: 一辆白色厢式车后门打开，里面堆着纸箱
scene: 楼下的面包车横在门口，后门敞开，两个工人开始往外搬成摞的纸箱。 The delivery van blocked the narrow street.
sceneCN: 这里 van 是「厢式货车、面包车」（第 1 个义项：运货或载人的封闭车辆）；句意为那辆送货车堵住了狭窄的街道。后门敞开、堆满纸箱的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 古英语中的同形词，义为「簸箕；风选工具」
同源家族词，义为「大篷车；房车」

senses.title: A covered vehicle for goods
senses.definition: a road vehicle with a roof and closed sides, used for carrying goods
senses.definitionCN: 有顶、两侧封闭、用于运货的公路车辆
senses.example: They moved the whole flat in one van.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一辆货车装下了整套公寓的东西。
senses.why: The clipped word keeps the covered body of the older caravan, and a covered body is what carries goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个截短词保留了 caravan 的带篷车身，而带篷的车身正是用来装货的。

senses.title: A vehicle for carrying people
senses.definition: a closed vehicle used to carry a small group of people
senses.definitionCN: 用于载少数人的封闭车辆
senses.example: A van takes the children to school each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早上有一辆面包车送孩子们上学。
senses.why: The same closed box that holds boxes can hold people, so the vehicle needs only seats instead of crates.
senses.whyCN: 同一只装货的封闭箱子也能装人，于是车里的纸箱换成座位就成了面包车。

senses.title: A railway carriage for luggage or parcels
senses.definition: in British English, a separate railway carriage for luggage, mail, or goods
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中指单独的行李、邮件或货物车厢
senses.example: Leave your cases in the guard's van.
senses.exampleCN: 把箱子放在列车员的行李车厢里。
senses.why: Railways named their goods and luggage cars after the road wagon, so a van on rails carries the same load.
senses.whyCN: 铁路把运货与载行李的车厢按公路货车的名字命名，于是铁轨上的 van 也装着同样的东西。

senses.title: A short form of caravan
senses.definition: in British use, the short form of caravan, a vehicle towed for holidays
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中为 caravan 的简称，指拖挂式假日房车
senses.example: They spent a wet week in a van by the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边的一辆房车里度过了一个阴雨周。
senses.why: Since van began as a clipping of caravan, the full word and the short one still overlap in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 既然 van 本来就是 caravan 的截短，全形与短形在英国口语里仍然交叠。

intro.en: A clipped form of caravan, which came to English from Persian by way of French and Latin.
intro.cn: caravan 的截短形式，而 caravan 是从波斯语经法语与拉丁语进入英语的。

items.en: Karwan named a company of merchants or pilgrims travelling together.
items.cn: karwan 指结队同行的商队或朝圣者。

items.en: Latin took the word as caravana, a group of travellers.
items.cn: 拉丁语取用为 caravana，指结队的旅人。

items.en: French caravane named both the travellers and the covered wagon they used.
items.cn: 法语 caravane 兼指旅队与他们所乘的带篷车。

items.en: English caravan comes to mean any covered wagon, and later a towed holiday home.
items.cn: 英语 caravan 先泛指带篷车，后来指拖挂的假日房车。

items.en: Van is the clipped form, first of caravan, then a word for a covered goods vehicle.
items.cn: van 是其截短形式，先指 caravan，后指有篷的运货车辆。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the caravan family the word was clipped from, and the near-meaning group places it by size and shape among other vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组收集 van 所从截出的 caravan 词族，近义组按大小与形状把它放在其他车辆之间。

normalIntro.en: Four letters for a box on wheels with a roof: something goes inside and moves.
normalIntro.cn: 四个字母，指一只装了轮子、盖了顶的箱子：东西装进去就运走。

normal.en: A removal van moves furniture, a delivery van brings parcels.
normal.cn: removal van 搬家具，delivery van 送包裹。

normal.en: The British luggage van means a railway carriage, not a road vehicle.
normal.cn: 英式的 luggage van 指铁路车厢，不是公路车辆。

normal.en: Van is short for caravan in British holiday talk.
normal.cn: 英式度假语境里 van 是 caravan 的简称。

normal.en: The plural is simply vans.

normal.cn: caravan 保留了较早的全形。

abstract.en: Picture back doors open and cardboard boxes piled inside.
abstract.cn: 想象后门打开，里面堆着纸箱。

abstract.en: Hear a van idle at dawn outside a bakery.
abstract.cn: 听黎明时面包店外一辆货车空转。

abstract.en: See children climb into a school van in the rain.
abstract.cn: 看孩子们在雨里钻进校车。

examples.en: The van was too high to enter the car park.
examples.cn: 那辆货车太高，进不了停车场。

examples.en: Two men carried the sofa out to the van.
examples.cn: 两个人把沙发抬到了货车上。

examples.en: The guard's van is at the back of the train.
examples.cn: 列车员的行李车厢在列车尾部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弯」——大车拐弯费劲，厢式车的「弯」也是它起名的一声。

root: van 为 caravan（大篷车）的截短形式，caravan 出自中世纪拉丁语 caravana，溯源为波斯语 karwan（结队的旅人）

sensesIntro.en: A covered wagon becomes a goods vehicle, then a people carrier, then a railway luggage car, and in Britain a shortened caravan.
sensesIntro.cn: 带篷车先成为运货车辆，再成为载人车辆，再成为铁路行李车厢，在英国还成了 caravan 的简称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white van with its back doors open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆白色厢式车后门敞开。

branches.en: The delivery branch: parcels in and out all day.
branches.cn: 配送分支：整天进进出出卖包裹。

branches.en: The passenger branch: a small group seated inside.
branches.cn: 乘客分支：车里坐着一小群人。

branches.en: The railway branch: cases ride in their own coach.
branches.cn: 铁路分支：箱子坐自己的车厢。

branches.en: The holiday branch: a towed caravan shortened.
branches.cn: 度假分支：拖挂房车的简称。

branches.en: The shape branch: a roof and closed sides define the van.
branches.cn: 形状分支：有顶有侧壁才是厢式车。

intro.en: A clipped word: caravan lost its head and kept its tail.
intro.cn: 一个截短词：caravan 丢掉了头，留下了尾。

latinIntro.en: The full form caravan came from Persian karwan through Latin and French; the four-letter van contains no separable Latin piece.
latinIntro.cn: 全形 caravan 经拉丁语与法语来自波斯语 karwan；四字母的 van 里已没有可拆的拉丁成分。

items.example: Van is complete on its own today.
Caravan survives beside the short form.

definition_zh: 防御；辩护；防务
definition_en: the act of guarding against attack; the case argued for an accused person
core_image: 城门紧闭，门后有人举着盾
scene: 石墙沿着山脊铺开，墙头还留着射箭的窄口。 The old wall was built for defence against northern raids.
sceneCN: 这里 defence 指「防御」（第 1 个义项：抵御进攻的行为）；句意是这道古墙是为防御北方袭扰而修的。

senses.title: Guarding against attack
senses.definition: the act of protecting a place or person from attack
senses.definitionCN: 保护地点或人物不受攻击的行为
senses.example: The old wall was built for defence against northern raids.
senses.exampleCN: 这道古墙是为防御北方袭扰而修的。
senses.why: A wall is a promise made before the enemy arrives.
senses.whyCN: 墙是在敌人到来之前就先许下的承诺。

senses.title: The case argued for the accused
senses.definition: the arguments and evidence given for a person in court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上为某人提出的理由与证据
senses.example: Her defence was that she had acted in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 她的辩护是当时一片漆黑才那样做。
senses.why: To defend a person in words is to stand in front of them again.
senses.whyCN: 用言语为人辩护，就是再一次站到他前面。

senses.title: The forces and works of a country
senses.definition: the armed forces and buildings that protect a country
senses.definitionCN: 保护一个国家的武装力量与设施
senses.example: The country spends a large share of its income on defence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家把很大一部分收入用在防务上。
senses.why: What protects a whole country turns from an act into a system.
senses.whyCN: 保护整个国家的行为，会从动作变成一套体系。

intro.en: Defence goes back to Latin defendere, to ward off, built from de- away and -fendere to strike.
intro.cn: defence 上溯到拉丁语 defendere（挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）组成。

items.en: Defendere meant to push a blow away from oneself.
items.cn: defendere 意为把打来的一击推开。

items.en: Defense carried the word into the language of law and war.
items.cn: defense 把这个词带进法律与战争的语言。

items.en: English used defence for both a shield and a plea.
items.cn: 英语用它同时指盾牌和申辩。

items.en: Spelling split, with defence in Britain and defense in America.
items.cn: 拼写分成两支，英国用 defence，美国用 defense。

items.en: Defence now also names a whole national system of protection.
items.cn: 如今它还可以指整套国家防护体系。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the same defe- shape, and the meaning group offers three words for keeping something safe.
note.cn: 形近组都绕着 defe- 这个形状，近义组则给出三种「护住」的说法。

entries.definition: the American spelling of this word
to win against an opponent
to put something off to a later time
the state of being kept safe
a person or act that keeps watch
entries.definitionCN: 看守的人或看守的行为

entries.definition: a flat object held to stop a blow

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a gate held shut and end with a lawyer standing up in court.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一扇紧闭的城门开始，落到法庭上站起来的那位律师。

normal.en: The best wall is the one the enemy never tries.
normal.cn: 最好的墙，是敌人根本不来试的那一道。

normal.en: A shield is heavy, and that weight is the point.
normal.cn: 盾很沉，沉就是它的意义。

normal.en: In court, defence means standing between a person and a sentence.
normal.cn: 在法庭上，辩护就是站在人和判决之间。

normal.en: One letter turns a lost battle into a wall that holds.
normal.cn: 差一个字母，打输的仗就变成了守住的墙。

normal.en: Spell it with c at home and with s across the sea.
normal.cn: 在本土写 c，在海那边写 s。

abstract.en: Picture a bar dropped across a door at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一根门闩落在门上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to stop a falling branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起来挡住落下的树枝。

abstract.en: Picture a man on his feet in a quiet room, speaking for another.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的屋里一个人站起来，替别人说话。

examples.en: The old wall was built for defence against northern raids.
examples.cn: 这道古墙是为防御北方袭扰而修的。

examples.en: She spoke in defence of the small library.
examples.cn: 她为这家小图书馆辩护。

examples.en: The team's defence held for the last ten minutes.
examples.cn: 球队的防线在最后十分钟守住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defence 记成「挡风死」：de 开头，fence 是篱笆，篱笆挡风又挡人，就是防御。

root: 源自拉丁语 defendere（把打击挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）合成，经古法语 defense 进入英语。它最早兼指盾牌与申辩，十七世纪后英式拼作 defence、美式拼作 defense，如今还引申为整个国家的防务体系。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall that holds, to a voice that answers in court, to a system that guards a country.
sensesIntro.cn: 从守得住的墙，到法庭上应答的声音，再到护卫一国的体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate shut with a shield behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：城门关上，门后有人举盾。

branches.en: The first sense is the physical act of keeping a blow away.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把打击挡在外面的实际动作。

branches.en: The same act in words becomes the case for the accused.
branches.cn: 同样的动作换成言语，就是为被告申辩。

branches.en: Repeated for a whole country, the act becomes an institution.
branches.cn: 为整个国家重复这个动作，它就成了制度。

branches.en: A wall and an army do the same job at different sizes.
branches.cn: 一道墙和一支军队，只是规模不同，做的是同一件事。

branches.en: Shield and argument both stand between a person and harm.
branches.cn: 盾与辩词，都挡在人和伤害之间。

intro.en: Defence gathers verbs, adjectives and nouns about guarding and about speaking up.
intro.cn: defence 聚起一族词：有保卫的动词，也有表示防护与申辩的形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is -fendere, to strike, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 -fendere（击打），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.example: They built a defence along the river.
items.exampleCN: 他们沿河修了一道防线。

items.example: He defended his friend in the meeting.
She is a defender of old trees.

items.exampleCN: 他的选择是站得住脚的。

items.example: The village lay defenceless in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 村庄在山谷里毫无防卫。

items.meaning: a lawyer who argues for the accused
items.example: The defence lawyer asked for time.
items.exampleCN: 辩护律师请求给些时间。

definition_zh: 农作物；收成；一批；剪短
definition_en: plants grown in large amounts for food, or the harvest they give
core_image: 一整片麦田在风里翻成金色的浪
scene: 风一吹，整片麦田翻成金色的浪。 The rice crop was the best in ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 crop 指「收成」（第 1 个义项：一季种出的农产品）；句意是这一季稻谷的收成是十年来最好的。

senses.title: Plants grown for food
senses.definition: plants grown in large amounts for food or for sale
senses.definitionCN: 大量种植以供食用或出售的植物
senses.example: Wheat is the main crop in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦是这个山谷的主要农作物。
senses.why: People choose what to plant, and the choice shapes a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 人决定种什么，而这个决定塑造了整片田。

senses.title: One season's harvest
senses.definition: the amount of food gathered from one season of growth
senses.definitionCN: 一季生长后收获的农产品数量
senses.example: The apple crop was small this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年苹果的收成很小。
senses.why: A whole summer is finally counted in one number.
senses.whyCN: 整个夏天，最后只被算成一个数字。

senses.title: A group appearing at once
senses.definition: a number of people or things that appear at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时出现的一批人或事物
senses.example: A new crop of students arrived in September.
senses.exampleCN: 九月来了一批新学生。
senses.why: New students come up together, like grain in one field.
senses.whyCN: 新生一起冒出来，就像同一片田里的庄稼。

intro.en: Crop comes from Old English cropp, the top or head of a plant.
intro.cn: crop 源自古英语 cropp，指植物的顶端或穗。

items.en: Cropp meant the top or head of a plant.
items.cn: cropp 指植物的顶端或穗头。

items.en: It also named a bird's craw.
items.cn: 它也指鸟的嗉囊。

items.en: Crop named the grain gathered from a field.
items.cn: crop 指从田里收上来的谷物。

items.en: It came to mean a whole season of harvest.
items.cn: 它开始指一整季的收成。

items.en: It was used for hair cut close to the head.
items.cn: 它被用来指剪得很短的头发。

items.en: It also means a group appearing at one time.
items.cn: 它也指同时出现的一批。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cropp- spelling, and the meaning group names other farm products.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cropp- 这串拼写，近义组列出其他农产说法。

entries.definition: cut short, or cut off at the edges
entries.definitionCN: 剪短的，或被裁去边缘的

entries.definition: a person who grows crops
land used for growing crops
the gathering in of a season's crops
entries.definitionCN: 把一季作物收上来的过程

entries.definition: food grown on a farm
the amount a field or farm gives
entries.definitionCN: 一块田或农场产出的数量

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a golden field and end with a new class in September.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一片金色的田开始，最后落到九月新来的一班学生。

normal.en: Crop is what the top of a plant becomes in our hands.
normal.cn: crop 就是植物顶端最终落到我们手里的东西。

normal.en: One summer becomes one number.
normal.cn: 一个夏天，最后变成一个数字。

normal.en: A cut of hair and a cut of grain share the word.
normal.cn: 剪头发和割庄稼，用的是同一个词。

normal.en: Problems crop up like weeds: suddenly, and in groups.
normal.cn: 麻烦像杂草一样冒出来：突然，而且成群。

normal.en: New students are a crop: they come up together.
normal.cn: 新生就是一批庄稼：一起冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture wheat bending in one long wave.
abstract.cn: 想象麦子弯成一道长长的浪。

abstract.en: Picture a hand full of fresh grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手捧着新收的谷粒。

abstract.en: Picture a gate full of new faces.
abstract.cn: 想象门口挤满新面孔。

examples.en: Farmers here grow three crops a year.
examples.cn: 这里的农民一年种三季作物。

examples.en: The corn crop survived the dry summer.
examples.cn: 玉米收成熬过了干旱的夏天。

examples.en: A new crop of problems cropped up at once.
examples.cn: 一批新问题一下子冒了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crop 记成从植物顶端割下来的那一把：一季的庄稼，就是收成。

root: 源自古英语 cropp（植物顶端、穗），后指从田里收上来的谷物，再引申为一季的收成、同时出现的一批，以及剪短的动作。

sensesIntro.en: From what grows in the field, to what the field gives, to a group that arrives together.
sensesIntro.cn: 从田里种的东西，到田里给出的收成，再到一起到来的一批。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field of wheat turning gold in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：风里翻成金色的麦田。

branches.en: The planted plants are the crop itself.
branches.cn: 种下去的植物本身就是作物。

branches.en: The gathered amount is the season's crop.
branches.cn: 收回来的数量，就是这一季的收成。

branches.en: A group arriving together borrows the field image.
branches.cn: 同时到来的一批，借用了田里的意象。

branches.en: What is planted and what is gathered share one word.
branches.cn: 种下的和收回的，共用一个词。

branches.en: Both a harvest and a class are counted as one lot.
branches.cn: 收成和一个班，都被算作一整批。

intro.en: Crop is a short Old English word that builds compounds like cropland and sharecropper.
intro.cn: crop 是古英语的短词，能组成 cropland、sharecropper 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin base is involved; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基，它是英语本族词。

items.example: The crop stood tall in June.

items.exampleCN: 这些田里种着两季作物。

items.meaning: the act of growing or cutting
a farmer who pays rent in crops
