definition_zh: 纯的；不掺杂的；纯粹的；纯理论的；纯洁的
definition_en: containing nothing except the stated substance, being nothing more than what is said, or studied without thought of practical use
core_image: 一只玻璃杯里的水清到能看见杯底纹路，旁边一滴墨也没落进去
scene: 实验台上摆着一只玻璃杯，里面的水清得能看见杯底的纹路，桌边连一滴墨水也没有。 The lab uses only pure water for this test, because any impurity would change the result.
sceneCN: 这里取「纯的、不掺杂的」（第 1 个义项：只含有所说的物质，没有杂质）；句意为实验室这项测试只用纯水，因为任何杂质都会改变结果。能看见杯底纹路的清水就是线索。

pos.zh: 纯的；不掺杂的；纯粹的；纯理论的；纯洁的

derivatives.zh: 由 pure 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「纯净；纯度」
由拉丁词干 pur- 加 -ify（源自 facere，做）构成，义为「净化；提纯」
由 pure 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「纯粹地；仅仅」
由 purify 加 -cation 构成，义为「净化；提纯」

senses.title: Not mixed with anything else
senses.definition: containing nothing except the stated substance, with no added or foreign matter
senses.definitionCN: 只含有所说的那种物质，没有添加物或外来杂质
senses.example: The spring behind the house still gives pure water.
senses.exampleCN: 屋后的泉水至今仍出清水。
senses.why: Latin purus described something clean and unmixed, so the word begins with a physical test: what is left when everything foreign has been taken out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 purus 指干净、不混杂的东西，所以这个词的起点是一次很具体的检验：把一切外来的东西去掉之后还剩下什么。

senses.title: Nothing more than what is stated
senses.definition: used to stress that something is only what it is said to be, with nothing else added
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事只是所说的那样，没有别的成分
senses.example: Winning the prize was pure luck, since he had entered at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 得奖纯属运气，因为他是最后一刻才报名的。
senses.why: Once no foreign substance is allowed in, the word can also refuse any hidden cause: pure luck means luck with nothing else mixed in, not even effort.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不允许掺入外来物质，这个词也能用来排除任何隐藏的原因：pure luck 就是运气里不掺别的东西，连努力都不算。

senses.title: Studied without a practical aim
senses.definition: of a subject or a study, done to understand it rather than to use it for a practical purpose
senses.definitionCN: 指学科或研究出于理解本身而做，而不是为了实际用途
senses.example: She chose pure mathematics over engineering because she liked proofs more than machines.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了纯数学而不是工程，因为她喜欢证明胜过机器。
senses.why: A pure science is separated from application the way pure water is separated from everything dissolved in it: the practical part has been filtered out.
senses.whyCN: 纯科学与应用分开，正如纯水与溶于其中的一切分开：实用的部分被滤掉了，剩下的是学科本身。

senses.title: Morally clean and innocent
senses.definition: free from evil or sexual suggestion, often used of a person, a heart or a motive
senses.definitionCN: 没有邪恶或色情意味的，常用于形容人、心灵或动机
senses.example: Her motives were pure, and nobody could accuse her of seeking money.
senses.exampleCN: 她的动机是纯洁的，谁也不能指责她图钱。
senses.why: The Latin word for physically clean slid into the moral field early, because a stain that can be washed off is an easy picture for guilt that can be removed.
senses.whyCN: 那个表示「物理上干净」的拉丁词很早就滑入道德领域，因为「能洗掉的污渍」是「能去除的罪责」现成的画面。

intro.en: Pure comes from Latin purus, clean and unmixed; Old French reshaped it before English took it, and the moral sense arrived early.
intro.cn: pure 来自拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）；古法语先把它改造过，随后英语借入，道德义很早就一并带了过来。

items.en: Purus meant clean and free from mixture; its deeper origin is uncertain, and a common guess links it to an old root for cleansing.
items.cn: purus 意为干净、不混杂；它更早的来源不确定，一般认为与一个表示「清洗」的古老词根有关。

items.en: Purus combined with facere, to make, giving purificare, to make clean, the source of purify and purification.
items.cn: purus 与 facere（做、使）结合成 purificare（使干净），是 purify 与 purification 的来源。

items.en: Old French kept pur for clean and unmixed and also used it for what is morally blameless.
items.cn: 古法语用 pur 表示干净、不混杂，也用它指道德上没有过失的。

items.en: Middle English pure carried both the physical and the moral sense and added the sense of nothing but.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pure 同时带着物理义与道德义，并加入了「只不过是」的意思。

items.en: Modern English spreads the word across water, motives, luck and mathematics, all of them versions of nothing added.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分摊到水、动机、运气和数学上，而这些全都是「没有添加」的不同版本。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for clean; the near-meaning group gathers words for being free of mixture or of any other cause.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「干净」形容词上的词；近义组收表示不含杂质或不受其他原因影响的词。

entries.definition: The state of being pure.
To remove what is not wanted from something.
entries.definitionCN: 除去某物中不需要的成分。

entries.definition: Someone who insists on the exact original standards of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持某领域原有纯正标准的人。

entries.definition: To claim to be or to mean something; the spelling is close, but this word comes from a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 声称是或意指某事；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Free from dirt or unwanted matter.
entries.definitionCN: 没有污垢或多余东西的。

entries.definition: Used to stress that something is nothing but what is named.
entries.definitionCN: 用来强调某事只是所说的那样。

entries.definition: Not combined with anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 没有与其他东西混合的。

entries.definition: Complete, with nothing added or limiting.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的，没有任何附加或限制的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adjective for clean and unmixed, and its family keeps moving outward from water to motives, to theory and to blame.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「干净、不混杂」的形容词上，同族词从水一路向动机、理论和过失扩展。

normal.en: Purus means clean and unmixed, so pure is a word about what has been removed as much as about what is there.
normal.cn: purus 意为干净、不混杂，所以 pure 既在说剩下的东西，也在说被去掉的东西。

normal.en: Purity adds -ity and names the state; purify adds -ify and names the act of making something clean.
normal.cn: purity 加 -ity 指状态，purify 加 -ify 指使某物变干净的动作。

normal.en: Pure science is not a science washed with water; it is study with the practical aim filtered out, the same picture applied to ideas.
normal.cn: pure science 不是用水洗过的科学，而是把实用目的滤掉的研究，是同一个画面用在观念上。

normal.en: Pure luck and pure gold use the same logic: nothing else is mixed in, whether the thing is metal or chance.
normal.cn: pure luck 与 pure gold 逻辑相同：不管那是金属还是运气，里面都没有掺别的东西。

normal.en: The moral sense is old, not modern: a stain that can be washed away has long been a picture for guilt that can be removed.
normal.cn: 道德义并不新：能洗掉的污渍，很久以来就是「能去除的罪责」的画面。

abstract.en: To call something pure is to make a claim about its edges: nothing outside has got in.
abstract.cn: 说某物纯，其实是在为它的边界作证：外面的东西没有进来。

abstract.en: A pure motive and a pure metal are judged by the same question, namely what else is present.
abstract.cn: 纯动机与纯金属要用同一个问题来判断，那就是里面还有什么别的东西。

abstract.en: The word keeps reminding us that purity is defined by absence, not by addition.
abstract.cn: 这个词一直提醒人：纯是由「没有什么」来定义的，而不是由「多了什么」。

examples.en: The spring behind the house still gives pure water.
examples.cn: 屋后的泉水至今仍出清水。

examples.en: Winning the prize was pure luck, since he had entered at the last minute.
examples.cn: 得奖纯属运气，因为他是最后一刻才报名的。

examples.en: She chose pure mathematics over engineering because she liked proofs more than machines.
examples.cn: 她选了纯数学而不是工程，因为她喜欢证明胜过机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「漂尔」——衣服漂洗到只剩清水，一点泡沫都没有，就是 pure。

root: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂），其更早来源不确定，一般认为与表示「清洗」的词根有关；经古法语 pur 进入英语。同族的 purity、purify 都出自 purus。

sensesIntro.en: The core is nothing foreign inside; the senses divide into a substance without mixture, a statement with nothing behind it, study without use, and a person without blame.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「里面没有外来的东西」；义项分成不掺杂的物质、背后别无他物的说法、不为实用的研究，以及没有过失的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of water so clear that the pattern on its bottom shows through, with not one drop of ink nearby.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯清到能看见杯底纹路的水，旁边一滴墨也没有。

branches.en: a glass of water clear down to the etched bottom
branches.cn: 一杯清到能看见杯底纹路的水

branches.en: a prize won on a ticket bought at the last minute
branches.cn: 最后一刻买票却中了奖

branches.en: a blackboard covered with a proof and no diagram
branches.cn: 写满证明、没画一张图的黑板

branches.en: a hand raised to swear that no money was wanted
branches.cn: 举手发誓不为钱的那只手

branches.en: a cup holding nothing but water and nothing else
branches.cn: 杯子里除了水什么都没有

intro.en: A Latin adjective for clean holds the word together, and Latin and English endings build the nouns of state and the verb of making clean.
intro.cn: 表示「干净」的拉丁语形容词支撑着这个词，拉丁语与英语的词尾再构成表示状态的名词和表示「使之干净」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin purus, clean and unmixed, the noun puritas, and the verb purificare are the direct sources of the English word and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）、名词 puritas 与动词 purificare 是英语这个词及其同族词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 公司；坚固的；坚定的；价格坚挺的
definition_en: a business company, solid and hard to move, strong and not likely to change, or stable in price
core_image: 握手的瞬间，掌心有力而稳定
scene: 她和我有力地握了握手。 She gave my hand a firm shake.
sceneCN: 这里 firm 是「坚固的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她和我有力地握了握手。

senses.title: Business company
senses.definition: a business organization or company
senses.definitionCN: 商业机构或公司
senses.example: She joined a law firm in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入了城里的一家律师事务所。
senses.why: This is the most common noun sense today.
senses.whyCN: 这是今天最常见的名词义项。

senses.title: Solid and stable
senses.definition: solid, steady, and not easy to move
senses.definitionCN: 结实、稳固、不易移动的
senses.example: She gave my hand a firm shake.
senses.exampleCN: 她和我有力地握了握手。
senses.why: The original sense is physical solidity.
senses.whyCN: 最初的义项是物理上的坚固。

senses.title: Strong and decided
senses.definition: strong and not likely to change
senses.definitionCN: 坚强且不易改变的
senses.example: He has a firm belief in honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚定地相信诚实。
senses.why: A solid grip becomes a solid belief.
senses.whyCN: 稳固的握持变成了稳固的信念。

senses.title: Stable in price
senses.definition: staying at a steady level, especially of prices
senses.definitionCN: 保持在稳定水平，尤指价格
senses.example: Prices remained firm during the holiday season.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间价格保持坚挺。
senses.why: A market can stand firm like a body.
senses.whyCN: 市场也能像人一样站稳。

intro.en: Firm comes from Latin firmus, strong and steady, through Old French ferme.
intro.cn: firm 源自拉丁语 firmus（坚固、稳定），经古法语 ferme 传入英语。

items.en: Firmus meant strong and steady.
items.cn: firmus 意为坚固而稳定。

items.en: Ferme meant solid or steadfast.
items.cn: ferme 意为坚固或坚定。

items.en: Firm meant solid and unyielding.
items.cn: firm 意为坚固而不屈。

items.en: Firm named a business house.
items.cn: firm 指商号或公司。

items.en: Firm described steady prices.
items.cn: firm 用来形容价格坚挺。

note.en: Firm is compared with similar-looking words and with words for companies and strength.
note.cn: 把 firm 与形近词以及表示公司和坚固的词作比较。

entries.definition: land for growing crops
a shape or document
a border or structure
a business organization
hard and firm
very determined

normalIntro.en: Firm starts as a solid grip and grows into a company that stands steady.
normalIntro.cn: firm 从牢固的握持出发，长成稳稳站立的公司。

normal.en: A firm handshake shows confidence.
normal.cn: 有力的握手显出自信。

normal.en: The mattress is firm and comfortable.
normal.cn: 这张床垫结实又舒服。

normal.en: She has a firm belief in fairness.
normal.cn: 她坚定地相信公平。

normal.en: The law firm hired a new clerk.
normal.cn: 律师事务所雇用了一名新职员。

normal.en: Prices stayed firm all summer.
normal.cn: 整个夏天价格都很坚挺。

abstract.en: What is firm can hold its shape under pressure.
abstract.cn: 坚固之物能在压力下保持形状。

abstract.en: A company is firm because people trust it to stand.
abstract.cn: 公司之所以稳固，是因为人们相信它站得住。

abstract.en: Conviction is a handshake with oneself.
abstract.cn: 信念，是与自己的一次握手。

examples.en: She gave my hand a firm shake.
examples.cn: 她和我有力地握了握手。

examples.en: Prices remained firm during the holiday season.
examples.cn: 节日期间价格保持坚挺。

dict_mnemonic.text: firm 源自拉丁语 firmus（坚固），核心义「站稳、不动摇」，后指公司。

root: 源自拉丁语 firmus（坚固、稳定），核心义「站得稳」。

sensesIntro.en: Firm means a company, something solid, a strong belief, or steady prices.
sensesIntro.cn: firm 意为公司、坚固的、坚定的或价格坚挺的。

core.en: Something that stands strong and does not give way.
core.cn: 站得稳、不轻易让步的事物。

branches.en: Physical solidity.
branches.cn: 物理上的坚固。

branches.en: Mental steadiness.
branches.cn: 精神上的坚定。

branches.en: A market that holds its level.
branches.cn: 保持水平位的市场。

branches.en: A business that stands under its name.
branches.cn: 以名号立于世的企业。

branches.en: A solid name becomes a solid company.
branches.cn: 可靠的名号成为可靠的公司。

intro.en: Firm is a Latin-rooted word that also builds verbs through prefixes.
intro.cn: firm 源自拉丁词根，也能通过前缀构成动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin firmus and firmare also gave confirm, affirm, and infirm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 firmus 与 firmare 也孕育了 confirm、affirm 和 infirm。

items.example: The bed is firmer than mine.
Use the firmest ground for the tent.
items.exampleCN: 把帐篷扎在最坚实的地面上。

items.example: The firmness of the ice surprised him.

definition_zh: 使有资格；取得资格；限定；修饰；达标晋级
definition_en: to give someone the right or ability to do something; to reach the standard needed for a job or a competition; to limit the meaning of a statement; to describe or modify a word
core_image: 考场门口一张刚盖章的证书，边角还带着新墨
scene: 考场外的走廊里，她反复翻着笔记，等最后一门成绩公布。 Only after passing that exam could she qualify as a nurse.
sceneCN: 这里 qualify 是「取得从业资格」（第 2 个义项：通过考核获得某种身份）；句意为只有通过那场考试，她才能取得护士资格。画面里可留意：走廊、翻旧的笔记、成绩榜。

pos.zh: 使有资格；取得资格；限定；修饰；达标晋级

derivatives.zh: qualify 去 y 加 -ication，指资格、资历或取得资格的过程
qualify 加 -ed 作形容词，指合格的、有限定条件的
qualify 加 -er，指预选赛，也指语法中起限定作用的词
dis- 与 qualify 结合，指取消某人已有的资格

senses.title: To give or have the right to something
senses.definition: to give someone the right to do or receive something, or to have that right because the conditions are met
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事或获得某物的权利，或因条件满足而拥有这种权利
senses.example: Two years of residence qualify you for the local pension.
senses.exampleCN: 居住满两年就有资格领取当地的养老金。
senses.why: The medieval Latin verb meant to mark a thing with a quality, and from marking came the sense of declaring that a person meets a required standard.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语动词本指给事物标上某种性质，从「标记」引申出「声明某人达到了规定标准」。

senses.title: To train and pass the tests for a profession
senses.definition: to complete the training and pass the examinations needed to work in a profession
senses.definitionCN: 完成培训并通过从业所需的考试
senses.example: She qualified as a pharmacist in only four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她只用四年就取得了药剂师资格。
senses.why: A profession demands proof of a quality, so the verb came to name the whole process of earning that proof.
senses.whyCN: 一种职业要求证明你具备某种素质，于是这个动词就用来指取得这份证明的全过程。

senses.title: To reach the next stage of a competition
senses.definition: to reach the standard needed to continue in a competition or to enter a final stage
senses.definitionCN: 达到继续参赛或进入决赛阶段所需的标准
senses.example: Only the top two teams qualify for the final.
senses.exampleCN: 只有排名前两位的队伍才能晋级决赛。
senses.why: A league sets a line that must be crossed, and crossing that line is described with the same word as meeting any standard.
senses.whyCN: 联赛会划出一条必须越过的线，越过这条线与达到任何标准都用同一个词来描述。

senses.title: To limit or modify a word
senses.definition: to add words that limit the meaning of a statement, or in grammar to describe another word
senses.definitionCN: 加上词语以缩小某个说法的范围，或在语法上修饰另一个词
senses.example: The adverb qualifies the verb that follows it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰它后面的动词。
senses.why: The oldest Latin sense was to assign a quality, and assigning a quality can narrow a meaning as easily as it can widen a right.
senses.whyCN: 最早的拉丁义项是「赋予某种性质」，而赋予性质既能扩大权利，也同样能缩小一个说法的范围。

intro.en: Qualify is built from Latin qualis, of what kind, and a form of facere, to make; medieval Latin qualificare meant to give a quality, and English took the word through French.
intro.cn: qualify 由拉丁语 qualis（何种的）与 facere（做）的一种形式构成；中世纪拉丁语 qualificare 意为赋予性质，英语经法语借入这个词。

items.en: Qualis was the question word for kind, meaning of what sort, and it also gave Latin qualitas, the word for a quality.
items.cn: qualis 是询问种类的疑问词，意为「何种的」，它还给出拉丁语 qualitas（性质）。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do, and it appears in a long series of Latin verbs that name the making of something.
items.cn: facere 意为做、制造，出现在一长串表示「造成某物」的拉丁动词里。

items.en: Qualificare combined the two: to assign a quality to something, and in legal use to limit or restrict a claim.
items.cn: qualificare 把两者结合：给某物标上性质；在法律用法中又指限定或缩小一项主张。

items.en: Old French qualifier carried the word into French with the sense of naming a quality and of making someone fit.
items.cn: 古法语 qualifier 把这个词带入法语，兼有「标明性质」与「使某人合格」两义。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb for rights, for professional training, for reaching a later round, and for grammar.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个动词指获得权利、完成职业训练、进入下一轮比赛，以及语法上的修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same Latin stem of kind and making; the near-meaning group collects verbs of granting rights, setting standards and limiting meaning.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干（种类与制造）上的形式；近义组收表示授予权利、设定标准与限定含义的动词。

entries.definition: A certificate or skill showing that a person meets a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人达到标准的证书或技能。

entries.definition: A match deciding who advances, or a word that limits another.
entries.definitionCN: 决定谁晋级的比赛，或限定另一词范围的词。

entries.definition: To take away someone's right to take part.
A feature of a person or thing that makes it what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或事物成其为自身的一种特性。

entries.definition: To state officially that someone meets a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明某人达到某个标准。

entries.definition: To give someone the right to something.
To change something slightly, or to limit its meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 略微改变某物，或缩小其含义。

entries.definition: To keep something within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物限制在一定范围内。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin question about kind to a Latin verb of making, so its oldest idea is to give something a kind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语中询问「何种」的词与表示制造的动词接在一起，所以它最古老的意思是「给某物一个种类」。

normal.en: Qualify joins a stem meaning of what kind with a verb meaning to make: to qualify is to give something a kind.
normal.cn: qualify 把表示「何种」的词干与表示制造的动词连起来：使合格就是给某物一个种类。

normal.en: Qualification adds -tion and names the paper or the state that proves a standard has been met.
normal.cn: qualification 加 -tion，指证明达标的那张纸或那种状态。

normal.en: Qualifier does two jobs: a team that advances, and a word that narrows another word.
normal.cn: qualifier 有两项职责：晋级的队伍，以及缩小另一词范围的词。

normal.en: Disqualify adds dis- and removes exactly the right that the base verb had granted.
normal.cn: disqualify 加 dis-，去掉的正是原动词所授予的那项权利。

normal.en: Qualify for names a benefit, while qualify as names an identity, which is why one takes for and the other takes as.
normal.cn: qualify for 指向一种待遇，qualify as 指向一种身份，所以一个用 for，一个用 as。

abstract.en: A qualification is a line drawn by others, and the verb describes both drawing it and crossing it.
abstract.cn: 资格是别人划下的一条线，而这个动词既描述划线，也描述越线。

abstract.en: Every right has a condition, and the word for meeting the condition is the same word for narrowing a claim.
abstract.cn: 每项权利都有条件，而「满足条件」与「缩小主张」用的竟是同一个词。

abstract.en: To qualify is to be judged enough by someone who has the power to decide what enough means.
abstract.cn: 取得资格，就是被某个有权定义「够」的人判定为够。

examples.en: A degree does not automatically qualify you for the job.
examples.cn: 有学位并不自动让你有资格做这份工作。

examples.en: He qualified as a lawyer last spring.
examples.cn: 他去年春天取得了律师资格。

examples.en: Please qualify your claim so that it is not read too broadly.
examples.cn: 请对你的说法加以限定，免得被理解得过宽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔立飞」——拿到证书那一刻，身价立刻往上飞，记住 qualify 是取得资格。

root: 拉丁语 qualis（何种的）+ facere（做）→ 中世纪拉丁语 qualificare（赋予性质、限定）→ 古法语 qualifier → 英语 qualify；同族有 quality、qualification。

sensesIntro.en: The core is assigning a kind or a standard; the senses divide into granting a right, earning a professional proof, meeting a competition line, and narrowing a meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是标定种类或标准；义项由此分为授予权利、取得职业证明、达到比赛门槛，以及缩小一个说法的范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly stamped certificate at an examination hall door, its ink still wet.
core.cn: 核心意象：考场门口一张刚盖章的证书，边角还带着新墨。

branches.cn: 一张盖章、能打开一扇门的表格

branches.cn: 最后一场考试后的医院走廊

branches.cn: 通向决赛的终点线

branches.cn: 一个缩小动词范围的副词

branches.en: the same proof asked for in law and in training
branches.cn: 法律与训练所要的同一份证明

intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中询问种类的疑问词、表示制造的动词、两者的中世纪复合形式，以及构成名词与否定动词的英语词缀共同支撑。

definition_zh: 样本；样品；试样；抽样；品尝
definition_en: a small part that shows what the whole is like; a specimen taken for testing; to take or try a small part of something
core_image: 从一整批货中取出一小份，用来代表全部
scene: 医生取了血液样本做检查。 The doctor took a blood sample for testing.
sceneCN: 这里 sample 是「样本、试样」（第 2 个义项）；句意：医生取了血液样本做检查。

senses.title: A small representative part
senses.definition: a small part of something that shows what the whole is like
senses.definitionCN: 能代表整体状况的一小部分
senses.example: The shop gives free samples of the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店免费提供茶叶样品。
senses.why: The core sense is a part standing for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是用部分代表整体。

senses.title: A specimen for testing
senses.definition: a small amount of a substance taken for scientific testing
senses.definitionCN: 为科学检测而取的一小份物质
senses.example: The lab analysed the water sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室分析了水样。
senses.why: The representative part is taken specifically for analysis.
senses.whyCN: 代表性的一小份被专门取出用于分析。

senses.title: To take or try a part
senses.definition: to take a small part of something, or to try a little of it
senses.definitionCN: 取一小部分，或少量尝试
senses.example: You can sample three dishes at the buffet.
senses.exampleCN: 自助餐上你可以品尝三道菜。
senses.why: The verb turns the small part into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把「取一小份」变成动作。

intro.en: Sample comes from Old French essample, from Latin exemplum.
intro.cn: sample 来自古法语 essample，源头是拉丁语 exemplum。

items.en: Exemplum means a copy or example.
items.cn: exemplum 意为副本或范例。

items.en: Essample carries the sense of a model.
items.cn: essample 带有「范本」之义。

items.en: The first syllable drops, giving sample.
items.cn: 首音节脱落，形成 sample。

items.en: Sample names goods shown to buyers.
items.cn: 早期现代英语中 sample 指给买家的货样。

items.en: Science adopts sample for tested specimens.
items.cn: 科学领域用 sample 指待检试样。

note.en: A sample represents a whole; a simple thing is easy to understand.
note.cn: sample 是代表整体的样本，simple 则是简单的。

entries.definition: easy to understand or do
more than enough
a comparison using like or as
an individual example for study
a thing that shows a general rule
a small copy or a typical pattern

normalIntro.en: A sample is a small piece that speaks for the whole.
normalIntro.cn: sample 是代表整体的那一小份。

normal.en: They handed out samples at the supermarket.
normal.cn: 他们在超市分发样品。

normal.en: The nurse took a blood sample.
normal.cn: 护士采了血样。

normal.en: We sampled the local food.
normal.cn: 我们品尝了当地食物。

normal.en: A random sample reduces bias.
normal.cn: 随机抽样能减少偏差。

normal.en: The sample size was too small.
normal.cn: 样本量太小了。

abstract.en: Picture one spoonful taken from a large pot.
abstract.cn: 想象从一大锅里舀出一勺。

abstract.en: Imagine a fabric swatch showing the whole cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布样代表整匹布。

abstract.en: Think of a taste as a tiny preview of a meal.
abstract.cn: 把一口品尝想成整顿饭的微缩预览。

examples.en: Please send us a sample of the fabric.
examples.cn: 请给我们寄一份布料样品。

examples.en: The survey used a sample of one thousand adults.
examples.cn: 这项调查抽取了一千名成年人作为样本。

examples.en: Visitors can sample local cheeses.
examples.cn: 游客可以品尝当地奶酪。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: sample 是 example 的姊妹词，都源于拉丁语 exemplum（范例），记住「取一份作范例」。

root: sample 经由古法语 essample 来自拉丁语 exemplum（范例、样本），首音节脱落形成现代拼写。

sensesIntro.en: Sample is a representative part, a tested specimen, or the act of trying a small amount.
sensesIntro.cn: sample 指代表性样本、检测用试样，或少量尝试的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small part standing for the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：以一小部分代表整体。

branches.en: The base sense is a part that represents the whole.
branches.cn: 基础义是代表整体的一部分。

branches.en: Science takes a specimen for analysis.
branches.cn: 科学取试样进行分析。

branches.en: The verb turns sampling into an action.
branches.cn: 动词义把取样变成动作。

branches.en: Shops let buyers sample what they sell.
branches.cn: 商店让买家试用所售之物。

branches.en: Testing and tasting both use a small part.
branches.cn: 检测与品尝都只取一小部分。

intro.en: Sample forms a compact family around taking or showing a small part.
intro.cn: sample 围绕「取一小份或展示一小份」形成紧凑词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin exemplum and its relatives lie behind sample and example.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exemplum 及其同族词是 sample 与 example 的源头。

items.meaning: a small part or to try one

items.exampleCN: 实验室收到了三个样本。

items.meaning: a person or device that samples
items.example: The air sampler ran all night.
We need to resample the soil.
items.exampleCN: 我们需要重新采集土壤样本。

items.meaning: a sample drawn from a sample
items.example: They drew a subsample for review.
items.exampleCN: 他们抽取子样本进行复核。

items.meaning: a survey of a selected group
items.example: The sample survey covered five cities.
items.exampleCN: 这项抽样调查覆盖了五个城市。

latinEntries.example: Exemplum is the source of sample.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exemplum 是 sample 的源头。
exemplaris 是 exemplary 的前身。
